title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第七十四: 循吏
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第七十四: 循吏 Volume 86 Biographies 74: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 先王疆理天下，司牧黎元，刑法以禁其奸，禮教以防其欲，雖為政以德，理實殊塗，百慮一致，在斯而已。

translations.literal: The ancient kings demarcated and governed the realm, tended and shepherded the common people, used penal law to restrain their wickedness, and used ritual instruction to guard against their desires. Though governing by virtue, the principles in truth followed different paths; a hundred considerations converged on one point—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings divided the land and ruled the world, caring for the common people. They employed criminal law to curb wrongdoing and ritual teaching to restrain excess desire. Though they governed through virtue, the practical means differed; yet every policy aimed at the same end—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 《書》云「知人則哲」，又云「無曠庶官」，言非其人為空官也。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says, "He who knows men is wise," and also says, "Do not let the multitude of offices go vacant"—meaning that when the wrong person holds a post, it is an empty office.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents states, "Knowing men is wisdom," and also warns, "Do not leave the offices vacant"—which is to say, an office held by the wrong man is no office at all.

sentences.zh: 睿哲之後，必致清明之臣；

translations.literal: After a sagacious and wise ruler, there will surely appear clear and upright ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Under a wise and perceptive sovereign, clear-minded and upright ministers inevitably appear;

sentences.zh: 昏亂之朝，多有貪殘之吏。

translations.literal: In a benighted and disorderly court, there are many greedy and cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt and chaotic court breeds greedy and brutal officials in abundance.

sentences.zh: 嗜欲所召，影響從之。

translations.literal: What appetites summon, shadows and echoes follow.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever a ruler's appetites call forth, imitators trail in their wake.

sentences.zh: 故五帝三王，不易人而化，皆在所由化之而已。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Emperors and Three Kings did not change men yet achieved transformation—all depended on whom they had to transform them.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and Three Kings transformed people without replacing them; everything hinged on who did the transforming.

sentences.zh: 蓋有無能之吏，無不可禦之人焉。

translations.literal: For there are incapable officials, but there are no people who cannot be governed.
translations.idiomatic: There may be incompetent officials, but there is no one beyond the reach of good governance.

sentences.zh: 自罷侯置守，歷年永久，統以方牧，仍世相循，所以寬猛為用，庇人調俗。

translations.literal: Since the abolition of feudal lords and the establishment of commanderies, years have passed in long succession; governing through regional inspectors continued generation after generation—thus leniency and severity were employed to shelter the people and harmonize custom.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since feudal domains were abolished and prefectural governors installed, the system of regional oversight has endured for generations, alternating severity and leniency to protect the people and shape local custom.

sentences.zh: 但廉平常跡，聲有難高；

translations.literal: But honest and ordinary conduct—its reputation is hard to raise high;
translations.idiomatic: Yet modest integrity wins little acclaim;

sentences.zh: 適時應務，招響必速。

translations.literal: Adapting to the times and responding to affairs—its summons and echo come swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: while timely boldness brings instant recognition.

sentences.zh: 是故搏擊為侯，起不旋踵；

translations.literal: Therefore those who strike hard become marquises, rising without turning the heel;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the forceful rose to noble rank overnight;

sentences.zh: 懦弱貽咎，錄用無時。

translations.literal: The weak and timid incur blame, and when recorded for appointment, there is no timely selection.
translations.idiomatic: the timid were blamed and passed over when offices were filled.

sentences.zh: 此則已然於前世矣！

translations.literal: This was already manifest in former ages!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the pattern long before our own day!

sentences.zh: 後之為吏，與世沈浮，叔季澆漓，奸巧多緒，居官蒞職，道各不同，故往籍述其賢能，以彰懲勸之道。

translations.literal: Later officials drifted with the age; in the declining season customs ran thin and deceitful schemes multiplied. Holding office and exercising duty—each followed a different path. Therefore past records set forth the worthy and capable to make manifest the way of reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations of officials rode the currents of their times; as the age declined, customs grew shallow and cunning multiplied. Men in office pursued divergent paths. That is why earlier annals recorded the worthy and capable—to illustrate how reward and punishment should work.

sentences.zh: 案魏立《良吏傳》有張恂、鹿生、張膺、宋世景、路邕、閻慶胤、明亮、杜纂、裴佗、竇瑗、羊敦、蘇淑。

translations.literal: Examining Wei: they established the "Biography of Good Officials" with Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, and Su Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei compiled a Biography of Good Officials including Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, and Su Shu.

sentences.zh: 齊立《循吏傳》有張華原、宋世良、郎基、孟業、崔伯謙、蘇瓊、房豹、路去病。

translations.literal: Qi established the "Biography of Virtuous Officials" with Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi compiled a Biography of Virtuous Officials including Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing.

sentences.zh: 《周書》不立此篇。

translations.literal: The Zhou History does not establish this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Zhou includes no such chapter.

sentences.zh: 隋《循吏傳》有梁彥光、樊叔略、趙軌、房恭懿、公孫景茂、辛公義、柳儉、劉曠、王伽、魏德深。

translations.literal: The Sui "Biography of Virtuous Officials" has Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Zhao Gui, Fang Gongyi, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, and Wei Deshen.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Biography of Virtuous Officials lists Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Zhao Gui, Fang Gongyi, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, and Wei Deshen.

sentences.zh: 其張恂、鹿生、宋世景、裴佗、羊敦、宋世良、郎基、崔伯謙、房豹、趙軌、房恭懿，各附其家傳，其餘皆依時代編緝，以備《循吏篇》云。

translations.literal: As for Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Song Shijing, Pei Tuo, Yang Dun, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Cui Boqian, Fang Bao, Zhao Gui, and Fang Gongyi—each is appended to his family biography; the rest are compiled by era to complete the chapter on virtuous officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Song Shijing, Pei Tuo, Yang Dun, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Cui Boqian, Fang Bao, Zhao Gui, and Fang Gongyi each appear in their family biographies; the remainder are arranged by period here to complete the chapter on virtuous officials.

sentences.zh: 張膺路邕閻慶胤明亮杜纂竇瑗蘇淑張華原孟業蘇瓊路去病梁彥光樊叔略公孫景茂辛公義柳儉郭絢敬肅劉曠王伽魏德深

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Dou Yuan, Su Shu, Zhang Huayuan, Meng Ye, Su Qiong, Lu Qubing, Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Guo Xun, Jing Su, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, Wei Deshen
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Dou Yuan, Su Shu, Zhang Huayuan, Meng Ye, Su Qiong, Lu Qubing, Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Guo Xun, Jing Su, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, Wei Deshen

sentences.zh: 張膺，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 延興中，為魯郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Yenxing era he served as Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yenxing period he served as prefect of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 履行貞素，妻女樵采自供。

translations.literal: His conduct was pure and simple; his wife and daughters gathered firewood to supply their needs.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with austere integrity; his wife and daughters gathered firewood to support the household.

sentences.zh: 孝文深嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deeply commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen greatly praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆太守，清白著稱，得吏人之忻心焉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Jingzhao, famed for integrity and clarity, and won the glad hearts of officials and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Jingzhao, he won renown for integrity and earned the affection of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 路邕，陽平人也。

translations.literal: Lu Yong was a man of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yong was a native of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，除東魏郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Xuanwu period he was appointed Administrator of Dongwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was appointed prefect of Dongwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 蒞政清勤。

translations.literal: When he took office his administration was pure and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was scrupulous and industrious.

sentences.zh: 經年儉，日出家粟，賑賜貧窘。

translations.literal: For years there was famine; each day he brought out grain from his household to relieve and bestow upon the poor and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Famine persisted for years; each day he distributed grain from his own household to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 靈太后下詔褒美，賜龍廄馬一匹、衣一襲、被褥一具。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict praising him, bestowing one horse from the imperial stud, one suit of clothing, and one set of bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict commending him and granted him a horse from the imperial stud, a suit of clothes, and bedding.

sentences.zh: 稍遷南青州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Governor of Southern Qing Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to governor of Southern Qing province, where he died.

sentences.zh: 閻慶胤，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qingyin—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qingyin's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 為東秦州敷城太守。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Fucheng in Eastern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Fucheng in Eastern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 頻年饑儉，慶胤歲常以家粟千石，賑恤貧窮，人賴以濟。

translations.literal: For successive years there was famine; each year Qingyin used a thousand piculs of household grain to relieve and succor the poor, and the people relied on him to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck year after year; each year Qingyin distributed a thousand piculs of his own grain to relieve the poor, and the people were sustained by his aid.

sentences.zh: 部人陽寶龍一千餘人申頌美政。

translations.literal: More than a thousand people of the commandery, led by Yang Baolong, submitted a memorial praising his excellent government.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand local men led by Yang Baolong petitioned to praise his good governance.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，靈太后卒無褒賞。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported this, but Empress Dowager Ling in the end granted no reward.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported this to the throne, but Empress Dowager Ling never issued a reward.

sentences.zh: 明亮，字文德，平原高昌人也。

translations.literal: Ming Liang, styled Wende, was a man of Gaochang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Liang, courtesy name Wende, was a native of Gaochang in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 有識幹，曆員外常侍。

translations.literal: He had insight and ability and served successively as an outer palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: A man of discernment and capacity, he rose through the outer palace attendant ranks.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，宣武臨朝堂，親自黜陟，授亮勇武將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang period Emperor Xuanwu came to the main hall in person to dismiss and promote officials, and appointed Liang Brave Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanchang, Emperor Xuanwu personally presided at court to promote and demote officials and appointed Liang general of brave martial valor.

sentences.zh: 亮進曰：「臣本官常侍，是第三清；

translations.literal: Liang advanced and said: "Your servant's original office was outer palace attendant, which is the third rank of clarity;
translations.idiomatic: Liang stepped forward and said, "Your servant's former post as outer palace attendant ranked among the third degree of clarity;

sentences.zh: 今授臣勇武，其號至濁。

translations.literal: now Your Majesty appoints your servant Brave Martial—the title reaches the turbid.
translations.idiomatic: yet Your Majesty now grants me the title of brave martial general, which ranks among the turbid.

sentences.zh: 且文武又殊，請更改授。」

translations.literal: Moreover civil and military are again different; I beg to change the appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military posts are distinct as well; I beg a different appointment."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「九流之內，人咸君子，卿獨欲乖眾，妄相清濁，所請未可。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Within the nine currents all men alike are gentlemen; you alone wish to defy the multitude, vainly distinguishing clarity from turbidity—the request cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Among all ranks of men, each is a gentleman in his way; you alone wish to stand apart from the crowd, arbitrarily dividing clear from turbid posts. Your request cannot be granted."

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「今江左未賓，書軌宜一，方為陛下投命前驅，拓定吳會。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Now the lands south of the Yangtze have not yet submitted; writing and ruts should be one. I am about to cast my life before Your Majesty as vanguard, to expand and settle Wu and Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "The lands south of the Yangtze have not yet submitted; the empire's roads and records should be unified. I am ready to risk my life as Your Majesty's vanguard to conquer Wu and Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 官爵，陛下之所輕；

translations.literal: Office and rank—Your Majesty holds them light;
translations.idiomatic: Titles and ranks Your Majesty holds lightly;

sentences.zh: 賤命，微臣之所重。

translations.literal: this humble life—your servant holds it heavy.
translations.idiomatic: this lowly life your servant holds dear.

sentences.zh: 陛下方收所重，何惜所輕？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is about to take what your servant holds heavy—why spare what Your Majesty holds light?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is about to accept what I hold dear—why begrudge what you hold cheap?"

sentences.zh: 因請改授平遠將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested instead the appointment of Pacification-at-a-Distance General.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked instead for appointment as general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「運籌用武，然後遠人始平。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Only after devising strategy and employing force do distant peoples begin to be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Only after strategy and arms are deployed are distant peoples pacified.

sentences.zh: 卿但用武平之，何患不得平遠乎？」

translations.literal: You need only use martial force to pacify them—what worry that you cannot obtain 'pacify the distant'?"
translations.idiomatic: Use military force to pacify them—why worry that you cannot also 'pacify the distant'?"

sentences.zh: 亮乃陳謝而退。

translations.literal: Liang then expressed thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thanked him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 除陽平太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 清白愛人，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Pure and clear, he loved the people and had excellent benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and compassionate, he governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 轉汲郡太守，為政如前，舉宣遠近。

translations.literal: Transferred to Administrator of Ji Commandery, his administration was as before, and his conduct was proclaimed far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Ji commandery, he governed as before, and his reputation spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 卒，二郡人吏迄今追思之。

translations.literal: When he died, the officials and people of both commanderies to this day still recall him with longing.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, officials and commoners in both commanderies still mourn him to this day.

sentences.zh: 杜纂，字榮孫，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Du Zuan, styled Rongsun, was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zuan, courtesy name Rongsun, was a native of Jiumen in Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以清苦自立。

translations.literal: In youth he established himself through hardship and purity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he distinguished himself through frugal integrity.

sentences.zh: 時縣令齊羅喪亡，無親屬收殮，纂以私財殯葬，由是郡縣標其門閭。

translations.literal: At that time the county magistrate Qi Luo died with no kin to collect and bury the body; Zuan buried him at private expense, and for this the commandery and county marked his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the county magistrate Qi Luo died without relatives to bury him, Zuan interred him at his own expense; the commandery and county honored his household gate for this deed.

sentences.zh: 後居父喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Later, in mourning for his father, he fulfilled every rite.
translations.idiomatic: Later he observed full mourning rites for his father.

sentences.zh: 郡舉孝廉，稍除積弩將軍，從征新野。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he was gradually appointed General of Accumulated Crossbows and followed the campaign against Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he was gradually promoted to general of accumulated crossbows and joined the campaign against Xinye.

sentences.zh: 及南陽平，以功賜爵井陘男。

translations.literal: When Nanyang was pacified, for his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanyang was pacified, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Jingxing for his merit.

sentences.zh: 賞帛五百匹，數日之中，散之知友，時人稱之。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with five hundred bolts of silk; within a few days he distributed them among his friends, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Awarded five hundred bolts of silk, he distributed them among his friends within days, winning praise throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 曆武都、漢陽二郡太守，並以清白為名。

translations.literal: He served successively as Administrator of Wudou and Hanyang, both offices famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Wudou and Hanyang, winning renown for integrity in both posts.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，拜清河內史。

translations.literal: In the early Ming period he was appointed Interior Minister of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming reign he was appointed interior minister of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，尤愛貧老，問人疾苦，至有對之泣涕。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and restrained, he especially loved the poor and elderly; inquiring into people's hardships, he sometimes wept in their presence.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he especially cared for the poor and elderly; when he heard of people's suffering he sometimes wept before them.

sentences.zh: 勸督農桑，親自檢視，勤者賞以物帛，惰者加以罪譴。

translations.literal: He urged and supervised agriculture and sericulture, personally inspecting; the diligent he rewarded with goods and silks, the idle he punished with censure.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted farming and sericulture, inspecting the fields himself; the diligent he rewarded with goods and cloth, the lazy he punished.

sentences.zh: 吊死問生，甚有恩紀。

translations.literal: Condoling the dead and inquiring after the living, he had great kindness and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted the bereaved and cared for the living with notable kindness and order.

sentences.zh: 除東益州刺史，無禦邊威略，群氐反叛，以失人和徵還。

translations.literal: Appointed Governor of Eastern Yi Province, he lacked frontier prestige and strategy; the various Di rebelled, and he was recalled for losing the people's support.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed governor of Eastern Yi province, he lacked frontier authority and strategy; when various Di groups rebelled he was recalled for failing to win people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遷太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand palace counselor.

sentences.zh: 正光末，清河人房通等三百人頌纂德政，乞重臨郡，詔許之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, three hundred men of Qinghe led by Fang Tong praised Zuan's virtuous government and begged that he return to the commandery; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang, three hundred Qinghe men led by Fang Tong praised Zuan's governance and petitioned for his return; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，為葛榮圍逼。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang period he was besieged by Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he was besieged by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 以郡降，榮以為常山太守。

translations.literal: He surrendered the commandery; Rong made him Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered the commandery; Ge Rong appointed him prefect of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 榮滅，卒於家。

translations.literal: When Rong was destroyed, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat he died at home.

sentences.zh: 纂所歷任，好行小惠，蔬食弊衣，多涉誣矯。

translations.literal: In every office Zuan held, he liked to perform small favors, ate vegetables and wore worn clothes, and often engaged in false display.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he favored small acts of kindness, ate plainly and dressed poorly, and often courted a reputation for austerity he did not fully earn.

sentences.zh: 而輕財潔己，終無受納，為百姓所思，號為良守。

translations.literal: Yet he was light with wealth and pure toward himself, and in the end accepted nothing—therefore the people thought of him and called him a good administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was generous with others and strict with himself, never accepting bribes; the people cherished him and hailed him a worthy magistrate.

sentences.zh: 天平中，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianping period he was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was posthumously enfeoffed as governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 竇瑗，字世珍，遼西陽洛人也。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan, styled Shizhen, was a man of Yangluo in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan, courtesy name Shizhen, was a native of Yangluo in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 自言本出扶風平陵，漢大將軍武曾孫崇為遼西太守，遂家焉。

translations.literal: He said of himself that his origin was Fufeng Pingling; the Han great general Dou Wu's great-grandson Chong was Administrator of Liaoxi and there established his house.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Pingling in Fufeng: Chong, great-grandson of the Han general Dou Wu, served as administrator of Liaoxi and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 曾祖堪，慕容氏漁陽太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kan was Administrator of Yuyang under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kan was administrator of Yuyang under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 祖表，馮弘城周太守，入魏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Biao was Administrator of Chengzhou under Feng Hong and entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Biao was administrator of Chengzhou under Feng Hong and entered Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 父冏，舉秀才，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Jiong, recommended as a cultivated talent, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiong, recommended as a cultivated talent, died young.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，瑗啟以身階級為父請贈，詔贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Putai period Yuan petitioned to use his own rank to request posthumous honors for his father; an edict enfeoffed the father posthumously as Governor of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putai, Yuan petitioned to use his own rank to secure posthumous honors for his father; the court enfeoffed his father posthumously as governor of Ping province.

sentences.zh: 瑗年十七，便荷帙從師，遊學十載，始為御史。

translations.literal: At seventeen Yuan shouldered his book bundle and followed teachers; after ten years of study he first became an imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he took up his satchel and studied under teachers; after ten years of learning he first became an imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 後兼太常博士，拜太原王爾硃榮官，榮留為北道大行台左丞。

translations.literal: Later he also served as a doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, received appointment from Prince Yuan of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong, and Rong retained him as left aide of the Northern Expedition Grand Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a doctor of the grand imperial sacrifices, accepted office from Prince Yuan of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong, and Rong kept him as left aide on the northern expedition grand commission.

sentences.zh: 以拜榮官，賞新昌男。

translations.literal: For accepting office from Rong he was rewarded with the title Baron of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: For accepting office under Rong he was enfeoffed as baron of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 從榮東平葛榮，封容城縣伯。

translations.literal: Following Rong east to pacify Ge Rong, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Following Rong east to suppress Ge Rong, he was enfeoffed as earl of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 瑗乞以容城伯讓兄叔珍，詔聽以新昌男轉授之。

translations.literal: Yuan begged to yield the earldom of Rongcheng to his elder brother Shuzhen; an edict allowed the barony of Xinchang to be transferred to him instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked to yield the earldom of Rongcheng to his elder brother Shuzhen; the court permitted the barony of Xinchang to be transferred to Shuzhen instead.

sentences.zh: 叔珍由是位至太山太守。

translations.literal: Shuzhen thereby rose to the post of Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhen thereby rose to prefect of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆等立長廣王曄為主，南赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong and others established Prince Ye of Changguang as ruler and marched south toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and others installed Prince Ye of Changguang as ruler and marched south toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至東郭外，世隆等遣瑗奏廢之，瑗執鞭獨入禁內，奏願行堯、舜事，曄遂禪廣陵。

translations.literal: Reaching the eastern suburb, Shilong and others sent Yuan to memorialize deposing him; Yuan took the whip and entered the inner palace alone, memorializing that he wished to carry out the affairs of Yao and Shun; Ye thereupon abdicated in favor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern suburb Shilong and others sent Yuan to memorialize for Ye's deposition; Yuan entered the inner palace alone with whip in hand, declaring he would enact the transfer of Yao and Shun; Ye then abdicated to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 由是除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: For this he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu he served as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he served as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 及釋奠開講，瑗與溫子升、魏季景、李業興並為擿句。

translations.literal: At the libation and opening of lectures, Yuan together with Wen Zisheng, Wei Jijing, and Li Yexing all composed extemporaneous verses.
translations.idiomatic: At the libation ceremony opening the lectures, Yuan joined Wen Zisheng, Wei Jijing, and Li Yexing in composing extemporaneous verses.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除廣宗太守，政有清白之稱。

translations.literal: In the Tianping period he was appointed Administrator of Guangzong, his government famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was appointed prefect of Guangzong, famed for upright governance.

sentences.zh: 廣宗人情凶戾，累政咸見告訟。

translations.literal: The people of Guangzong were by nature fierce and cruel; successive administrations all faced accusations and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's people were fierce by nature; every previous administration faced lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 唯瑗一人，終始全潔。

translations.literal: Yuan alone, from beginning to end, remained entirely unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan alone remained unstained from first to last.

sentences.zh: 轉中山太守，聲譽甚美，為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: Transferred to Administrator of Zhongshan, his reputation was very fine, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhongshan, he won an excellent reputation and the affection of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武班書州郡，稱瑗政績，以為勸勵。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu circulated documents to the commanderies and provinces praising Yuan's achievements, it served as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi Shenwu circulated documents to commanderies and provinces praising Yuan's achievements, it served as encouragement to others.

sentences.zh: 後授平州刺史，在州政如臨郡。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Ping Province; in the province his government was as when he administered a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed governor of Ping province, he governed the province with the same care he had shown in commandery office.

sentences.zh: 又為神武丞相府右長史。

translations.literal: He also served as right chief clerk of Shenwu's chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as right chief clerk in Shenwu's chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 瑗無軍府斷割才，不甚稱職。

translations.literal: Yuan lacked talent for military headquarters decisions and adjudication, and did not quite fit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan lacked the decisiveness needed in a military headquarters and did not quite suit the post.

sentences.zh: 又行晉州事。

translations.literal: He also administered Jin Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also handled affairs in Jin province.

sentences.zh: 及還鄴，上表曰：「臣伏讀《麟趾新制》至三公曹第六十六條：'母殺其父，子不得告，告者死。'

translations.literal: When he returned to Ye, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has read the New Regulations of the Linzhi, to Article 66 of the Three Excellencies Bureau: 'If a mother kills her husband, the son may not accuse her; whoever accuses her dies.'
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Ye he submitted a memorial: "Your servant has read the New Regulations of the Linzhi, Article 66 of the Three Excellencies Bureau: 'If a mother kills her husband, the son may not accuse her; whoever accuses her dies.'

sentences.zh: 三返覆之，未得其門。

translations.literal: Three times I have turned it over and still cannot find the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Three times I have pondered it and still cannot grasp its meaning.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 案律：'子孫告父母、祖父母者，死。'

translations.literal: Examining the statutes: 'If sons or grandsons accuse parents or grandparents, they die.'
translations.idiomatic: The statutes state: 'Sons or grandsons who accuse parents or grandparents shall die.'

sentences.zh: 又漢宣云：'子匿父，孫慝大父母，皆勿論。'

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'If a son conceals his father, or a grandson conceals his grandparents, none shall be prosecuted.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han also said: 'If a son conceals his father, or a grandson conceals his grandparents, none shall be prosecuted.'

sentences.zh: 蓋謂父母、祖父母小者攘羊，甚者殺害之類，恩須相隱，律抑不言，法理如是，足見其直，未必指母殺父，止子不言也。

translations.literal: This generally means that when parents or grandparents commit minor offenses such as stealing sheep, or serious ones such as killing people, affection requires mutual concealment; the law suppresses speech—legal principle is thus, which fully shows its rightness. It need not refer only to a mother killing the father while the son remains silent.
translations.idiomatic: This generally covers cases where parents or grandparents commit minor offenses such as stealing sheep or serious ones such as murder—family affection requires mutual concealment, and the law forbids disclosure. The principle is sound and need not refer solely to a mother killing the father while the son remains silent.

sentences.zh: 今母殺父而子不告，便是知母而不知父，識比野人，義近禽獸。

translations.literal: Now if a mother kills the father and the son does not report it, this is knowing the mother but not knowing the father—understanding comparable to wild men, righteousness close to beasts.
translations.idiomatic: If a mother kills the father and the son does not report it, he knows his mother but not his father—understanding fit for savages, conduct close to beasts.

sentences.zh: 且母之于父，作合移天，既殺己之天，復殺子之天，二天頓毀，豈容頓默？

translations.literal: Moreover the mother toward the father is a union that shifts heaven; having killed one's own heaven, she again kills the son's heaven—two heavens suddenly destroyed—how can sudden silence be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: A wife's bond to her husband is a union that shifts heaven itself; having destroyed her own heaven, she destroys her son's heaven as well—two heavens shattered at once. How can silence be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 此母之罪，義在不赦；

translations.literal: This mother's crime—in righteousness she should not be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Such a mother's crime admits no pardon in righteousness;

sentences.zh: 下手之日，母恩即離。

translations.literal: on the day she struck, maternal affection was already severed.
translations.idiomatic: the day she struck, maternal affection was already severed.

sentences.zh: 仍以母道不告，鄙臣所以致惑。

translations.literal: Yet because of the way of the mother one does not report—this is why your humble servant is perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the law forbids reporting because she is one's mother—this is what perplexes your humble servant.

sentences.zh: 如或有之，可臨時議罪，何用豫制斯條，用為訓誡？

translations.literal: If such cases exist, guilt may be debated when they occur—why use this article in advance as instruction and admonition?
translations.idiomatic: If such cases arise, guilt may be debated when they occur—why encode this provision in advance as a standing rule?

sentences.zh: 恐千載之下，談者喧嘩，以明明大朝，有尊母卑父之論。

translations.literal: I fear that a thousand years hence talkers will clamor, saying that this illustrious great dynasty had a doctrine honoring the mother and demeaning the father.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that a thousand years hence people will clamor that this illustrious dynasty honored mothers and demeaned fathers.

sentences.zh: 以臣管見，實所不取。」

translations.literal: In your servant's narrow view, this truly cannot be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: In your servant's humble view, this cannot be accepted."

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 三公郎封君義立判云：「母殺其父，子復告母，母由告死，便是子殺。

translations.literal: A gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau, Feng Junyi, drafted a judgment saying: "If a mother kills her husband and the son again accuses the mother, the mother dies because of the accusation—this is in effect the son killing her.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Junyi of the Three Excellencies Bureau drafted a judgment: "If a mother kills her husband and the son accuses her, the mother dies from the accusation—in effect the son kills her.

sentences.zh: 天下未有無母之國，不知此子，將欲何之？

translations.literal: There has never been a realm without mothers—where would such a son go?
translations.idiomatic: No realm exists without mothers—where would such a son go?

sentences.zh: 既于法無違，於事非害，宣佈有司，謂不宜改。」

translations.literal: Since the law is not violated and the matter does no harm, it should be proclaimed to the offices that it ought not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Since the law is not violated and no harm is done, the offices should be told the statute ought not be changed."

sentences.zh: 瑗復難云：「局判雲'母由告死，便是子殺。

translations.literal: Yuan again objected, saying: "The bureau's judgment says 'the mother dies because of the accusation—this is in effect the son killing her.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan objected again: "The bureau's judgment says 'the mother dies from the accusation—in effect the son kills her.

sentences.zh: 天下未有無母之國，不知此子，將欲何之。'

translations.literal: There has never been a realm without mothers—where would such a son go?'
translations.idiomatic: No realm exists without mothers—where would such a son go?'

sentences.zh: 瑗案典律，未聞母殺其父而子有隱母之義。

translations.literal: Yuan examines the canonical statutes and has not heard of a meaning whereby a son may conceal a mother who killed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan examines the canonical statutes and finds no provision allowing a son to conceal a mother who killed his father.

sentences.zh: 既不告母，便是與殺父同。

translations.literal: If he does not report the mother, this is the same as not reporting the killing of the father.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to report the mother is the same as complicity in the father's murder.

sentences.zh: 天下可有無父之國，此子獨得有所之乎？」

translations.literal: Can there be a realm without fathers? Could this son alone have somewhere to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Can there be a realm without fathers? Could this son alone find refuge anywhere?"

sentences.zh: 事雖停寢。

translations.literal: Though the matter was suspended and set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was suspended and set aside.

sentences.zh: 除大宗正卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 宗室及其寒士，相與輕之，瑗案法推正，甚見仇疾。

translations.literal: The imperial clan and its poor and humble members together slighted him; Yuan pressed cases according to law and was greatly hated.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan and its poor relations slighted him together; Yuan pressed cases according to law and earned bitter enmity.

sentences.zh: 官雖通顯，貧窘如初，清尚之操，為時所重。

translations.literal: Though his office was eminent and visible, he was poor and distressed as at first; his pure and lofty conduct was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank was eminent, he remained as poor as ever; his integrity was valued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 領本州大中正，兼廷尉卿，卒官。

translations.literal: He held the post of chief rectifier of his native province and concurrently Minister of Justice, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief rectifier of his native province and concurrently as minister of justice, dying in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太僕卿、濟州刺史，諡曰明。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of the Imperial Stud and Governor of Ji Province, posthumous title Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed as minister of the imperial stud and governor of Ji province, with the posthumous title Ming.

sentences.zh: 蘇淑，字仲和，武邑人也。

translations.literal: Su Shu, styled Zhonghe, was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shu, courtesy name Zhonghe, was a native of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 兄壽興，坐事為閹官，後拜河間太守，賜爵晉陽男。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shouxing, because of an offense became a eunuch official; later appointed Administrator of Hejian, enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shouxing, punished for an offense, became a eunuch official; later he was appointed prefect of Hejian and enfeoffed as baron of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及壽興將卒，遂冒養淑為子。

translations.literal: When Shouxing was about to die, he falsely adopted Shu as his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxing was dying, he falsely adopted Shu as his son.

sentences.zh: 淑熙平中襲其爵。

translations.literal: In the Xiping period Shu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiping, Shu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後除樂陵內史，在郡綏撫，甚有人譽。

translations.literal: Later appointed Interior Minister of Leling; in the commandery he pacified and comforted, winning great popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed interior minister of Leling, where he governed with notable popular esteem.

sentences.zh: 後謝病乞解，有詔聽之，人吏老幼訴乞淑者甚眾。

translations.literal: Later he requested leave on grounds of illness; an edict permitted it, but old and young officials and people petitioned begging for Shu in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He later requested leave for illness; the court assented, but multitudes of officials and commoners petitioned for his return.

sentences.zh: 後曆滎陽、中山二郡太守，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Administrator of Xingyang and Zhongshan and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as prefect of Xingyang and Zhongshan, then died.

sentences.zh: 淑清心愛下，所曆三郡，皆為吏人所思，當時稱為良二千石。

translations.literal: Shu had a pure heart and loved those below him; in every commandery of the three he held office, officials and people cherished him, and the age called him a good two-thousand-bushel official.
translations.idiomatic: Pure-hearted and caring toward subordinates, in all three commanderies he won officials' and people's affection and was hailed a model prefect.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈衛大將軍、都官尚書、瀛州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: In the early Wuding period posthumously enfeoffed as Grand General of the Guard, Minister of the Court for State Affairs, and Governor of Ying Province, posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand general of the guard, minister of the court for state affairs, and governor of Ying province, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 齊神武追美清操，與羊敦同見優賞。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu posthumously praised his pure conduct, and together with Yang Dun he received preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi Shenwu posthumously praised his integrity; he and Yang Dun received special commendation together.

sentences.zh: 張華，原字國滿，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, original name Guoman, was a man of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, original name Guoman, was a native of Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少明敏，有器度。

translations.literal: In youth he was bright and keen, with capacity and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bright and keen, a man of capacity and breadth.

sentences.zh: 初為齊神武驃騎府法曹參軍，賜爵新城伯，累遷大丞相府屬。

translations.literal: At first he served as legal affairs officer in Shenwu's Rapid Cavalry headquarters, enfeoffed as Baron of Xincheng, and was promoted repeatedly to staff of the great chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as legal affairs officer in Shenwu's rapid cavalry headquarters, was enfeoffed as baron of Xincheng, and rose repeatedly on the great chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 深被親待，每號令三軍，恆令宣諭意旨。

translations.literal: Deeply trusted and favored, whenever orders were issued to the three armies he was always made to proclaim the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply trusted, whenever orders went to the three armies he was charged with proclaiming the commander's intent.

sentences.zh: 尋除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 周文始據雍州，神武使華原入關說焉。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen first held Yong Province, Shenwu sent Huayuan into the Pass to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wen first seized Yong province, Shenwu sent Huayuan through the pass to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 周文謂曰：「若能屈驥足於此，當共用富貴；

translations.literal: Zhou Wen said to him: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs here, we shall share wealth and honor together;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen told him: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs to stay here, we shall share wealth and honor;

sentences.zh: 不爾，命懸今日。」

translations.literal: otherwise your life hangs on this day."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise your life ends today."

sentences.zh: 華原曰：「殞首而已，不敢聞命。」

translations.literal: Huayuan said: "Death of the head only—I dare not hear the command."
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan replied: "I would lose my head before obeying such a command."

sentences.zh: 周文嘉其亮正，乃使東還。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen commended his integrity and forthrightness and sent him back east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen admired his integrity and sent him back east.

sentences.zh: 尋悔，遣追不及。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and sent pursuers, but they did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and sent pursuers, but they failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 神武以華原久而不返，每嘆惜之，及聞其來，喜見於色。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Huayuan had long not returned, sighed with regret each day; when he heard of his coming, his joy showed in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sighed daily over Huayuan's long absence; when news came of his return, joy showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 後除相府右長史，遷驃騎大將軍、特進，進爵為公，仍徙封新安。

translations.literal: Later appointed right chief clerk of the chancellor's office, promoted to Rapid Cavalry Grand General and Special Advance, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, and the fief was transferred to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed right chief clerk of the chancellor's office, promoted to rapid cavalry grand general and special advance, advanced to duke, and his fief transferred to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 後為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 華原有幹略，達政體。

translations.literal: Huayuan had resourcefulness and understood the substance of government.
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan was resourceful and understood governance in substance.

sentences.zh: 至州，乃廣布耳目，以威禁。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he widely deployed informants to enforce awe and prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the province he deployed informants widely to enforce law and order.

sentences.zh: 境內大賊及鄰州亡命三百餘人，皆詣華原歸款。

translations.literal: Within the borders, great bandits and more than three hundred fugitives from neighboring provinces all came to Huayuan to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Within the borders, major bandits and more than three hundred fugitives from neighboring provinces all came to Huayuan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 咸撫以恩信，放歸田里，於是人懷感附，寇盜寢息。

translations.literal: He comforted them all with kindness and trust and released them to return to their hamlets; thereby people's hearts attached in gratitude and bandits and robbers ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them all with kindness and trust and released them to their villages; people's hearts turned to him in gratitude and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 州獄先有系囚千餘人，華原科簡輕重，隨事決遣。

translations.literal: In the provincial prison there were formerly more than a thousand prisoners held; Huayuan classified light and heavy offenses and decided each according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial prison had held more than a thousand prisoners; Huayuan classified offenses by severity and disposed of each case accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至年暮，唯有重罪者數十人。

translations.literal: By year's end only several dozen remained for serious crimes.
translations.idiomatic: By year's end only several dozen serious offenders remained.

sentences.zh: 華原各給假五日，曰：「期盡速還也。」

translations.literal: Huayuan gave each five days' leave, saying: "When the term ends, return swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan granted each five days' leave, saying: "Return promptly when the term ends."

sentences.zh: 囚等曰：「有君如是，何忍背之！」

translations.literal: The prisoners said: "With a lord like this, how could we bear to betray him!"
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners said: "With a lord like this, how could we betray him!"

sentences.zh: 依期畢至。

translations.literal: They all returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: They all returned on schedule.

sentences.zh: 先是，州境數有猛獸為暴。

translations.literal: Before this, within the province fierce beasts had repeatedly ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Previously fierce beasts had repeatedly ravaged the province.

sentences.zh: 自華原臨政，州東北七十里甑山中，忽有六駮食猛獸，咸以為化感所致。

translations.literal: From the time Huayuan took office, in Zeng Mountain seventy li northeast of the province seat, six piebald beasts suddenly appeared eating fierce beasts—all regarded this as an effect of transformation and influence.
translations.idiomatic: After Huayuan took office, six piebald beasts appeared in Zeng Mountain seventy li northeast of the seat, devouring the fierce beasts—people took this as proof of his transforming influence.

sentences.zh: 卒官，州人大小莫不號慕，為樹碑立祠，四時祭焉。

translations.literal: He died in office; people of the province great and small all wailed and admired him, erecting a stele and shrine, with sacrifices in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; people throughout the province mourned him, erected a stele and shrine, and offered seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works and Left Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed as duke of the ministry of works and left vice minister of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子宰均嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zaijun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zaijun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孟業，字敬業，钜鹿安國人也。

translations.literal: Meng Ye, styled Jingye, was a man of Anguo in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ye, courtesy name Jingye, was a native of Anguo in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本寒微，少為州吏，性廉謹。

translations.literal: His family was originally humble and slight; in youth he was a provincial clerk, by nature honest and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: His family was humble; in youth he served as a provincial clerk, honest and cautious by nature.

sentences.zh: 同僚諸人，侵盜官絹，分三十匹與業，拒而不受。

translations.literal: Fellow clerks all embezzled official silk; they divided thirty bolts and gave them to Ye, but he refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow clerks embezzled official silk and offered him thirty bolts; he refused them.

sentences.zh: 行台郎中郭秀相禮接，方欲薦之，會秀卒。

translations.literal: The expeditionary staff gentleman Guo Xiu treated him with courtesy and was about to recommend him when Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu of the expeditionary staff treated him courteously and was about to recommend him when Xiu died.

sentences.zh: 魏彭城王韶，齊神武之婿也，拜定州刺史，除業為典簽。

translations.literal: Wei Prince Shao of Pengcheng, son-in-law of Qi Shenwu, was appointed Governor of Ding Province and made Ye his master of records.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Pengcheng in Wei, son-in-law of Qi Shenwu, was appointed governor of Ding province and made Ye his master of records.

sentences.zh: 長史劉仁之謂業曰：「我處其外，君居其內，同心戮力，庶有濟乎？」

translations.literal: The chief administrator Liu Renzhi said to Ye: "I am on the outside, you on the inside—if we join hearts and exert our strength together, might there be success?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Liu Renzhi told Ye: "I stand outside, you inside—if we join forces, might we succeed?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，仁之入為中書令，臨路啟韶云：「殿下左右可信任者，唯有孟業，願專任之，餘人不可信也。」

translations.literal: Before long Renzhi entered office as Director of the Imperial Secretariat; on the road he memorialized to Shao: "Among those around Your Highness who can be trusted, only Meng Ye—Your Highness should entrust him exclusively; the rest cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Renzhi became director of the imperial secretariat; leaving, he memorialized to Shao: "Of those around Your Highness, only Meng Ye can be trusted—entrust him exclusively; the rest cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 又與業別，執手曰：「令我出都，君便失援，恐君在後，不自保全，唯正與直，願君自勉。」

translations.literal: He also took leave of Ye, grasping his hand and saying: "Now that I leave the capital, you will lose support; I fear that afterward you cannot preserve yourself—only uprightness and integrity do I wish you to strive for."
translations.idiomatic: He also bade Ye farewell, grasping his hand: "Leaving the capital, you lose your support; I fear you cannot protect yourself afterward—strive only for uprightness and integrity."

sentences.zh: 業唯有一馬，瘦死。

translations.literal: Ye had only one horse, which died thin.
translations.idiomatic: Ye owned only one horse, which died emaciated.

sentences.zh: 韶以業貧，令州府官人，同食馬肉，欲令厚相酬償。

translations.literal: Shao, because Ye was poor, ordered provincial and commandery officials to eat the horse's meat together, wishing to have them compensate him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Ye's poverty, Shao ordered provincial officials to share the horse's meat, intending that they compensate him generously.

sentences.zh: 業固辭不敢。

translations.literal: Ye firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ye firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 韶乃戲業曰：「卿邀名人也。」

translations.literal: Shao then jested with Ye: "You invite famous men."
translations.idiomatic: Shao then jested: "You court famous men."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「業為典簽，州中要職，諸人欲相賄贍，止患無方便耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Ye serves as master of records, a key post in the province; the others wish to bribe me and only lack a convenient means.
translations.idiomatic: Ye replied: "As master of records I hold a key provincial post; others wish to bribe me and only lack opportunity.

sentences.zh: 今喚食肉，恐致聚斂，有損聲名，所以仰違明教。」

translations.literal: Now summoning them to eat meat, I fear it will lead to extortion and harm my reputation; therefore I respectfully disobey your enlightened order."
translations.idiomatic: Summoning them to eat horse meat may lead to extortion and harm my reputation; therefore I respectfully disobey."

sentences.zh: 後未旬日，韶左右王四德、董惟金並以馬死托肉，為長史裴英起密啟。

translations.literal: Within ten days afterward, Shao's attendants Wang Side and Dong Weijin both used the dead horse's flesh as a pretext; the chief administrator Pei Yingqi secretly memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Shao's attendants Wang Side and Dong Weijin both used the horse meat as a pretext; chief administrator Pei Yingqi secretly memorialized against Ye.

sentences.zh: 神武有書與韶，大致誚讓。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent a letter to Shao largely reproaching and blaming him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu wrote to Shao largely reproaching him.

sentences.zh: 業尋被譖，出外行縣事。

translations.literal: Ye was soon slandered and sent out to conduct county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was soon slandered and sent out to handle county affairs.

sentences.zh: 後神武書責韶云：「典簽姓孟者，極能用心，何乃令出外也！」

translations.literal: Later Shenwu wrote reproaching Shao: "The master of records surnamed Meng is extremely devoted—why did you send him outside!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Shenwu wrote reproaching Shao: "Master of records Meng is extremely devoted—why did you send him out!"

sentences.zh: 及韶代下，業亦隨還，贈送一無所受。

translations.literal: When Shao was replaced and left office, Ye also returned with him, accepting nothing from gifts and send-offs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao left office, Ye returned with him and accepted nothing from farewell gifts.

sentences.zh: 仁之後為西兗州，臨別謂吏部郎中崔暹曰：「貴州人士，唯有孟業，銓舉之次，不可忘也。」

translations.literal: When Renzhi later served Western Yan Province, on parting he told the Ministry of Personnel gentleman Cui Xian: "Among the gentlemen of your noble province, only Meng Ye—in order of selection he must not be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: When Renzhi later served in western Yan province, he told Cui Xian of the ministry of personnel: "Among your province's gentlemen, only Meng Ye—in ranking appointments do not forget him."

sentences.zh: 暹問業曰：「君往在定州，有何政，使劉西兗如此欽歎？」

translations.literal: Xian asked Ye: "When you were in Ding Province before, what government made Liu of Western Yan admire you so?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked Ye: "What governance in Ding province made Liu of western Yan admire you so?"

sentences.zh: 業答曰：「唯知自修也。」

translations.literal: Ye replied: "I only know self-cultivation."
translations.idiomatic: Ye replied: "I only cultivated myself."

sentences.zh: 韶為并州刺史，業復為典簽，仍兼長史。

translations.literal: Shao became Governor of Bing Province; Ye again served as master of records and concurrently chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shao became governor of Bing province; Ye again served as master of records and concurrently chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，清河王岳拜司州牧，召為法曹。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao period Prince Yue of Qinghe was appointed Governor of Si Province and summoned Ye as legal affairs officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, Prince Yue of Qinghe was appointed governor of Si province and summoned Ye as legal affairs officer.

sentences.zh: 業形貌短小，及謁見，嶽心鄙其眇小，笑而不言。

translations.literal: Ye's physique was short and small; on audience Yue inwardly despised his diminutive size and laughed without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was short in stature; at audience Yue inwardly despised his small frame and laughed without speaking.

sentences.zh: 後尋業斷決處，謂曰：「卿斷決之明，可謂有過軀貌之用。」

translations.literal: Later when he sought Ye's decisions, he said: "The clarity of your judgments can be said to have use beyond bodily appearance."
translations.idiomatic: Later, reviewing Ye's judgments, he said: "Your clarity exceeds what your stature suggests."

sentences.zh: 補河間王國郎中令。

translations.literal: Appointed gentleman of the interior of the Principality of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman of the interior of the principality of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 清貧自守，未曾有失。

translations.literal: Pure and poor, he guarded himself and never had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and poor, he guarded his integrity without fault.

sentences.zh: 文宣謂侍中裴英起曰：「卿識河間王郎中孟業不？

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan said to Attendant Pei Yingqi: "Do you know Meng Ye, gentleman of the interior of the Principality of Hejian?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan asked Attendant Pei Yingqi: "Do you know Meng Ye, gentleman of the interior of Hejian?

sentences.zh: 一昨見其國司文案，似是好人。」

translations.literal: Yesterday I saw his principality's official documents—they seem to be a good man."
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I saw his principality's documents—he seems a good man."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔與臣同事魏彭城王元韶。

translations.literal: He replied: "In former days I served together with him under Wei Prince Yuan Shao of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pei replied: "I once served with him under Prince Yuan Shao of Pengcheng in Wei.

sentences.zh: 其人清忠正直，世所稀有。」

translations.literal: This man is pure, loyal, upright, and honest—rare in the age."
translations.idiomatic: He is pure, loyal, upright, and honest—a rarity in our age."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如公言者，比來便是大屈。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "As you say, in recent times this has been a great injustice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "As you say, he has recently suffered a grave injustice."

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Writing draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed draftsman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宣初唯得姓名，及因奏事，見其羸老，又質性敦樸，無升降之容，加之平緩，寡於方便。

translations.literal: At first Wenxuan had known only his name; when he reported on affairs he saw Ye was frail and old, his nature plain and unassuming, without rising and falling in demeanor; moreover he was even-tempered and lacked artifice.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wenxuan knew only his name; when Ye reported on affairs the emperor saw he was frail and aged, plain and unassuming in manner, without courtly affectation, even-tempered and artless.

sentences.zh: 有一道士由吾道榮以術藝被迎，將入內，業為通名。

translations.literal: A Daoist, Youwu Daorong, was welcomed for his arts and was about to enter the palace; Ye announced his name.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Youwu Daorong was summoned for his arts and was about to enter the palace; Ye announced him.

sentences.zh: 忽於眾中抗聲奏云：「由吾道士不食五穀。」

translations.literal: Suddenly before the assembly he raised his voice and memorialized: "Daoist Youwu does not eat the five grains."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Ye raised his voice before the assembly: "Daoist Youwu does not eat grain."

sentences.zh: 帝命推而下之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him pushed down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him dragged from the hall.

sentences.zh: 又令點檢百官，敷奏失所，帝遣人以馬鞭擊業頭，至於流血。

translations.literal: He also ordered a review of all officials' memorials for improprieties; the Emperor sent men to strike Ye on the head with a horsewhip until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered officials' memorials reviewed for improprieties; the emperor had men strike Ye's head with a horsewhip until he bled.

sentences.zh: 然亦體其衰老，非力所堪。

translations.literal: Yet he also considered his old age and that he lacked the strength to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also considered Ye's age and that he could not bear such punishment.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，累遷東郡太守，以寬惠著名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian he was promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Dongjun, famed for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he rose to prefect of Dongjun, famed for leniency and kindness.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，五官張凝因出使，得麥一莖五穗，其餘或三穗四穗共一莖者，合郡咸以政化所感，因即申上。

translations.literal: That summer the Five Offices officer Zhang Ning, on a mission, obtained one stalk of wheat with five ears; others had three or four ears on one stalk; the whole commandery regarded it as a response to his transforming government and reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Zhang Ning of the Five Offices, on a mission, found wheat with five ears on one stalk; others had three or four; the commandery took this as proof of his governance and reported it.

sentences.zh: 至秋，復有東燕縣人班映祖，送嘉禾一莖九穗。

translations.literal: In autumn a man of Dongyan County, Ban Yingzu, presented a stalk of auspicious grain with nine ears.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Ban Yingzu of Dongyan county presented a stalk of auspicious grain with nine ears.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，敕人間養驢，催買甚切。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing an edict ordered the people to raise donkeys; the pressure to purchase was severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing an edict ordered households to raise donkeys; the pressure to buy them was severe.

sentences.zh: 業曰：「吾既為人父母，豈可坐看此急。

translations.literal: Ye said: "Since I am father and mother to the people, how can I sit and watch this urgency?
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "As father and mother to the people, how can I sit by while they are pressed?

sentences.zh: 令宜權出庫錢，貸人取辦，後日有罪，吾自當之。」

translations.literal: For the moment let treasury funds be advanced on loan to help people comply; if there is guilt later, I myself will bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Let treasury funds be loaned for now so people can comply; if guilt follows, I will bear it myself."

sentences.zh: 後為憲司所劾。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached by the inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later the inspectorate impeached him.

sentences.zh: 被攝之日，郡人皆泣而隨之，迭相吊慰。

translations.literal: On the day he was summoned, people of the commandery wept and followed him, condoling one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned, commandery people wept and followed him, comforting one another.

sentences.zh: 送業度關者，有數百人，至黎陽郡西，方得辭決。

translations.literal: Several hundred escorted Ye to the pass; only west of Liyang commandery could they take leave.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred escorted him to the pass; only west of Liyang could they bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 攀援號哭，悲動行路。

translations.literal: Clinging and wailing, their grief moved passersby.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging and wailing, they moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 詣闕訴冤者非一人，敕乃放還。

translations.literal: Those who went to the capital to plead injustice were not alone; an edict then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Many went to the capital to plead his case; an edict then released him.

sentences.zh: 郡中父老，扣河迎接。

translations.literal: The elders of the commandery met him at the river to welcome him back.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery elders met him at the river to welcome him home.

sentences.zh: 武成親戎，自洛還鄴，道由東郡。

translations.literal: Wucheng personally led the army; returning from Luoyang to Ye he passed through Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng led the army in person; returning from Luoyang to Ye he passed through Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 業具牛酒，率人吏拜謁路旁，自稱：「糞土臣孟業，伏惟聖駕親行，有征無戰，謹上微禮。」

translations.literal: Ye prepared oxen and wine and led officials and people to bow and greet him beside the road, saying of himself: "This worthless subject Meng Ye humbly observes that Your Sacred Majesty campaigns in person with victory unblooded—I present this slight gift."
translations.idiomatic: Ye prepared oxen and wine and led officials and people to bow beside the road, saying: "This worthless subject Meng Ye observes Your Majesty's campaign, victory without battle—I offer this humble gift."

sentences.zh: 便與人吏俱唱萬歲，導引前入，帝大嘉之。

translations.literal: He and the officials and people together shouted ten thousand years and guided the procession forward; the Emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people shouted long life and guided the procession; the emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 後除廣平太守，年既老，理政不如在東郡時。

translations.literal: Later appointed Administrator of Guangping; as he was old, his governance was not as in Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed prefect of Guangping; aged, he governed less well than in Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 武平九年，為太中大夫，加衛將軍，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wuping he was appointed Grand Palace Counselor and Guard General, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wuping he became grand palace counselor and guard general, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 業志守質素，不尚浮華。

translations.literal: Ye aspired to guard plain integrity and did not esteem ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Ye held to plain integrity and disdained display.

sentences.zh: 為子結婚，為朝肺腑吒羅氏。

translations.literal: When arranging his son's marriage, it was with the imperial in-law Tuo clan.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged his son's marriage with the imperial in-law Tuo clan.

sentences.zh: 其子以廕得為平原王段孝先相府行參軍，乃令作今世服飾綺襦紈袴。

translations.literal: His son, ennobled as staff officer in the chancellor's office of Prince Xiaoxian of Pingyuan, Duan Xiaoxian, had contemporary fashionable brocade jackets and silk trousers made.
translations.idiomatic: His son, a staff officer in Prince Xiaoxian of Pingyuan's chancellor's office, had fashionable brocade jackets and silk trousers made.

sentences.zh: 吒羅家又恃姻婭，炫曜矜誇。

translations.literal: The Tuo family again relied on the marriage tie, showing off and boasting.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuo family flaunted the marriage connection with boastful display.

sentences.zh: 業知而不禁，素望頗貶。

translations.literal: Ye knew yet did not forbid it; his longstanding reputation was somewhat diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Ye knew yet did not forbid it; his long-standing reputation suffered somewhat.

sentences.zh: 蘇瓊，字珍之，長樂武強人也。

translations.literal: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, was a man of Wuqiang in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qiong, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was a native of Wuqiang in Changle commandery.

sentences.zh: 父備，仕魏，至衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: His father Bei served Wei as far as Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bei served Wei as vice minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 瓊幼時隨父在邊，嘗謁東荊州刺史曹芝，芝戲問曰：「卿欲官不？」

translations.literal: In childhood Qiong followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou Inspector Cao Zhi; Zhi asked playfully: "Do you want an office?"
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Qiong followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi, who asked playfully: "Do you want an office?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「設官求人，非人求官。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Offices are established to seek men, not men to seek offices."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Offices are established to seek men, not men to seek offices."

sentences.zh: 芝異其對，署為府長流參軍。

translations.literal: Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi marveled and appointed him senior adjutant in his office.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄以儀同開府，引為刑獄參軍，每加勉勞。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang, holding the rank of palace guard of the fifth order, opened a staff office and made him penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging and commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wenxiang, as palace guard of the fifth order, opened a staff and made him penal-affairs officer, often encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 并州嘗有強盜，長流參軍張龍推其事，所疑賊徒，並已拷伏，失物家並識認，唯不獲盜贓。

translations.literal: In Bing Province there were once bandits; the senior adjutant Zhang Long investigated and had the suspected thieves all tortured into confession; the victims' households all identified them, yet the stolen goods were not recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bing province once had bandits; senior adjutant Zhang Long had suspects tortured into confession and victims identified them, yet the loot was not recovered.

sentences.zh: 文襄付瓊，更令窮審，乃別推得元景融等十餘人，並獲贓驗。

translations.literal: Wenxiang handed the case to Qiong for renewed investigation; he separately identified Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others and obtained the stolen goods as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang gave the case to Qiong, who identified Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others and recovered the loot.

sentences.zh: 文襄大笑，語前妄引賊者曰：「爾輩若不遇我好參軍，幾致枉死。」

translations.literal: Wenxiang laughed greatly and said to those who had wrongly implicated the thieves: "If you had not met my good staff officer, you would nearly have died unjustly."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang laughed and told those who had wrongly implicated men: "Had you not met my good staff officer, you would nearly have died unjustly."

sentences.zh: 除南清河太守。

translations.literal: Appointed Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 郡多盜賊，及瓊至，奸盜止息。

translations.literal: The commandery had many bandits; when Qiong arrived, wickedness and theft ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had many bandits; when Qiong arrived, theft ceased.

sentences.zh: 或外境奸非，輒從界中行過者，無不捉送。

translations.literal: If wicked men from outside the borders passed through the territory, none escaped capture and delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals from outside who passed through his territory were all captured and sent on.

sentences.zh: 零陵縣人魏雙成，住處與畿內武城交錯，失牛，疑其村人魏子賓，列送至郡。

translations.literal: A man of Lingling County, Wei Shuangcheng, lived where the border met Wucheng in the capital district; he lost an ox and suspected his fellow villager Wei Zibin, who was sent to the commandery under accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuangcheng of Lingling county, on the border with capital Wucheng, lost an ox and accused Wei Zibin, who was sent to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 一經窮問，知賓非盜，而便放之。

translations.literal: After one thorough inquiry he knew Zibin was not the thief and released him.
translations.idiomatic: One thorough inquiry showed Zibin was not the thief and he was released.

sentences.zh: 雙成云：「府君放賊去，百姓牛何處可得？」

translations.literal: Shuangcheng said: "The prefect has released the thief—where will the common people's cattle come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuangcheng said: "The prefect released the thief—where will people get their cattle back?"

sentences.zh: 瓊不理其語，密遣訪獲盜者。

translations.literal: Qiong paid no heed to his words and secretly sent men to find and capture the real thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong ignored him and secretly found the real thieves.

sentences.zh: 從此畜牧不收，云：「但存府君。」

translations.literal: From then on livestock was not penned in; people said: "Just leave it for the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter people did not pen livestock, saying: "Just leave it for the prefect."

sentences.zh: 其鄰郡富家，將財物寄置界內以避盜。

translations.literal: Wealthy families in neighboring commanderies deposited goods within his border to avoid thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy neighbors deposited goods in his territory to escape thieves.

sentences.zh: 冀州繹幕縣人成氏大富，為賊攻急，告曰：「我物已寄蘇公矣」，賊遂去。

translations.literal: A rich man of Yimo county in Ji Province, the Cheng clan, was hard pressed by bandits and said: "My goods are already with Lord Su"—the bandits then left.
translations.idiomatic: A rich Cheng clan in Yimo county, pressed by bandits, said: "My goods are with Lord Su"—and the bandits departed.

sentences.zh: 平原郡有妖賊劉黑苟，構結徒侶，通於滄海。

translations.literal: In Pingyuan Commandery there was a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, who formed a gang communicating with the Bohai Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan had a demonic bandit, Liu Heigou, who formed a gang linked to the Bohai coast.

sentences.zh: 瓊所部人，連接村居，無相染累。

translations.literal: People in Qiong's jurisdiction lived in connected villages and were not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Villages in his jurisdiction were connected yet none were implicated.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑於此伏其德績。

translations.literal: Neighboring counties at this bowed to his virtue and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring counties revered his virtue and achievements.

sentences.zh: 郡中舊賊一百餘人，悉充左右，人間善惡及長吏飲人一杯酒，無不即知。

translations.literal: More than a hundred old bandits in the commandery were all made his attendants; good and evil among the people and even when a superior drank one cup of wine—none escaped his knowledge at once.
translations.idiomatic: He made more than a hundred old bandits his attendants; he instantly knew good and evil among the people and even when superiors drank a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 瓊性清慎，不發私書。

translations.literal: Qiong was by nature pure and cautious and did not send private letters.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and cautious by nature, he sent no private letters.

sentences.zh: 道人道研為濟州沙門統，資產巨富，在郡多出息，常得郡縣為征。

translations.literal: The Daoist Daoyan was monastic superintendent of Jizhou, with vast wealth, lending at interest in the commandery, often having the commandery and counties collect for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Daoyan, monastic superintendent of Jizhou, was vastly wealthy and lent at interest, often having counties collect for him.

sentences.zh: 及欲求謁，度知其意，每見則談問玄理。

translations.literal: When he wished an audience, Qiong knew his intent and each time they met discussed metaphysics.
translations.idiomatic: When he sought an audience Qiong knew his intent and discussed metaphysics instead.

sentences.zh: 研雖為債數來，無由啟口。

translations.literal: Though Daoyan came many times on debt business, he had no opening to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Though Daoyan came repeatedly about debts, he never found an opening.

sentences.zh: 其弟子問其故，研曰：「每見府君，徑將我入青雲間，何由得論地上事。」

translations.literal: His disciples asked the reason; Daoyan said: "Each time I see the prefect he carries me straight into the blue clouds—how can I discuss earthly affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: His disciples asked why; Daoyan said: "Each audience the prefect carries me into the clouds—how can I discuss earthly affairs?"

sentences.zh: 師徒還歸，遂焚責券。

translations.literal: Master and disciples returned and burned the loan contracts.
translations.idiomatic: Master and disciples returned and burned the loan contracts.

sentences.zh: 郡人趙潁，官至樂陵太守，年余八十，致事歸。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Zhao Ying, rose to Administrator of Leling, over eighty years old when he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ying of the commandery rose to prefect of Leling and retired past eighty.

sentences.zh: 五月中，得新瓜一雙，自來奉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he brought a pair of new melons and came in person to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he brought new melons and presented them in person.

sentences.zh: 潁恃年老，苦請，遂便為留。

translations.literal: Ying relied on his old age and pressed hard; Qiong finally kept them.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pressed hard on account of his age; Qiong finally accepted.

sentences.zh: 乃致于査事梁上，竟不割。

translations.literal: He hung them on the investigation beam and in the end did not cut them.
translations.idiomatic: He hung them on the investigation beam and never cut them.

sentences.zh: 人聞受趙潁餉瓜，欲貢新果，至門，問知潁瓜猶在，相顧而去。

translations.literal: When people heard he had received Zhao Ying's melons and wished to bring new fruit, reaching the gate they learned Ying's melons were still there and looked at one another and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he had accepted Zhao Ying's melons, gift-bearers reached the gate, saw the melons still hanging, and left.

sentences.zh: 有百姓乙普明，兄弟爭田，積年不斷，各相援據，乃至百人。

translations.literal: A commoner, Yi Puming, and his brothers disputed fields, unresolved for years, each relying on backers until nearly a hundred people were involved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Puming and his brothers disputed fields for years, each gathering backers until nearly a hundred were involved.

sentences.zh: 瓊召普明兄弟，對眾人諭之曰：「天下難得者兄弟，易求者田地。

translations.literal: Qiong summoned the Puming brothers and before the crowd instructed them: "What the world can scarcely obtain is brothers; what is easy to obtain is land.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong summoned them and said before the crowd: "Brothers are hard to find; land is easy to find.

sentences.zh: 假令得地失兄弟心，如何？」

translations.literal: Suppose you gain land but lose brotherly hearts—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: If you gain land but lose brotherly affection, what then?"

sentences.zh: 因而下淚，諸證人莫不灑泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he shed tears; none of the witnesses did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: He wept; none of the witnesses failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 普明兄弟叩頭，乞外更思，分異十年，遂還同住。

translations.literal: The Puming brothers kowtowed and begged to reconsider; after ten years apart they returned to live together.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers kowtowed and asked to reconsider; separated ten years, they lived together again.

sentences.zh: 每年春，總集大儒衛覬隆、田元鳳等講於郡學，朝吏文案之暇，悉令受書。

translations.literal: Each spring he gathered great Confucians Wei Kilong, Tian Yuanfeng, and others to lecture at the commandery school; in their spare time from documents he had all clerks study books.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring he gathered great scholars to lecture at the commandery school and had clerks study in spare moments.

sentences.zh: 時人指吏曹為學生屋。

translations.literal: People of the time called the clerks' quarters the students' house.
translations.idiomatic: People called the clerks' quarters the students' house.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祠，婚姻喪葬，皆教令儉而衷禮。

translations.literal: He prohibited illicit shrines; in marriage and funerals he taught economy within proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He banned illicit shrines and taught frugal yet proper marriage and funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 又蠶月預下綿絹度樣於部內，其兵賦次第，並立明式。

translations.literal: In the silkworm month he sent down silk and gauze patterns in advance within the jurisdiction; military levies were also given clear forms.
translations.idiomatic: Before the silkworm month he distributed silk and gauze patterns; military levies had clear forms.

sentences.zh: 至於調役，事必先辦，郡縣吏長，恆無十杖稽失。
