translations.literal: As for corvée and levies, matters were always prepared in advance; commandery and county clerks never had ten blows of the staff for delay.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée and levies were always prepared in advance; clerks never suffered ten strokes for delay.

sentences.zh: 當時州郡，無不遣人至境，訪其政術。

translations.literal: At the time no province or commandery failed to send men to the border to study his methods of government.
translations.idiomatic: Every province and commandery sent men to study his governance.

sentences.zh: 天保中，郡界大水，人災，絕食者千餘家。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period great flood struck the commandery; more than a thousand households lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao great flood struck; more than a thousand households lacked food.

sentences.zh: 瓊普集郡中有粟家，自從貸粟，悉以給付饑者。

translations.literal: Qiong generally gathered households in the commandery with grain and himself borrowed grain to give to the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered households with grain and borrowed grain himself to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 州計戶徵租，復欲推其貸粟，綱紀謂瓊曰：「雖矜饑餒，恐罪累府君。」

translations.literal: The province calculated households to levy rent and also wished to press the borrowed grain; the clerk said to Qiong: "Though you pity the starving, I fear guilt will fall on the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: The province wished to levy rent and also press the borrowed grain; a clerk warned: "Though you pity the starving, guilt may fall on you."

sentences.zh: 瓊曰：「一身獲罪且活千室，何所怨乎？」

translations.literal: Qiong said: "If one body is guilty yet a thousand households live, what is there to resent?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said: "If I alone am guilty yet a thousand households live, what resentment is there?"

sentences.zh: 遂上表陳狀，使檢皆免，人戶保安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial stating the facts, and inspections exempted all; households were secure.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized; inspections exempted all and households were secure.

sentences.zh: 此等相撫兒子，咸言「府君生汝」。

translations.literal: Such people cherished him as sons, all saying "the prefect gave you birth."
translations.idiomatic: People cherished him as a father, saying "the prefect gave you birth."

sentences.zh: 在郡六年，人庶懷之，遂無一人經州。

translations.literal: In the commandery six years the people cherished him; not one person went to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Six years in office the people cherished him; not one petitioned the province.

sentences.zh: 前後四表，列為尤最。

translations.literal: Four times in succession he was listed in memorials as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Four memorials listed him as foremost.

sentences.zh: 遭憂解職，故人贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: When mourning relieved him of office, gifts from old friends—he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended his office, he accepted no gifts from old friends.

sentences.zh: 尋起為司直、廷尉正，朝士嗟其屈，尚書辛術曰：「既直且正，名以定體，不慮不申。」

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Minister of Justice rectifier; court gentlemen sighed at his demotion; Minister Xin Shu said: "Upright and correct—the name fixes the substance; no worry he will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as director of the imperial secretariat and rectifier of the minister of justice, courtiers sighed at his demotion; Xin Shu said: "Upright and correct—his name fits; he will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 初，瓊任清河太守，裴獻伯為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier when Qiong served as Administrator of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier as prefect of Qinghe, Pei Xianbo was governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 獻伯酷于用法，瓊恩於養人。

translations.literal: Xianbo was harsh in applying the law; Qiong was kind in nurturing people.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbo was harsh in law; Qiong kind in nurturing people.

sentences.zh: 房延祐為樂陵郡，過濟州。

translations.literal: Fang Yanyou was Administrator of Leling and passed through Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanyou was prefect of Leling and passed through Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 裴問其外聲，延祐云：「唯聞太守善，刺史惡。」

translations.literal: Pei asked his outside reputation; Yanyou said: "I only hear the prefect is good and the governor is bad."
translations.idiomatic: Pei asked his reputation abroad; Yanyou said: "I only hear the prefect is good and the governor bad."

sentences.zh: 裴云：「得人譽者非至公。」

translations.literal: Pei said: "One whom people praise is not perfectly fair."
translations.idiomatic: Pei said: "Popular praise is not perfect fairness."

sentences.zh: 答云：「若爾，黃霸、襲遂，君之罪人也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "If so, Huang Ba and Xi Sui are your guilty men."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If so, Huang Ba and Xi Sui are your guilty men."

sentences.zh: 後有敕，州各舉清能。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict that each province recommend the pure and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered each province to recommend the pure and capable.

sentences.zh: 裴以前言，恐為瓊陷，瓊申其枉滯，議者尚其公平。

translations.literal: Pei, because of the earlier words, feared framing Qiong; Qiong reported his wrongful detention and discussants admired his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Pei feared framing Qiong because of earlier words; Qiong reported his wrongful detention and discussants admired his fairness.

sentences.zh: 畢儀雲為御史中丞，以猛暴任職，理官忌憚，莫敢有違。

translations.literal: Bi Yiyun was Imperial Censor; fierce and violent in office, legal officials feared him and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yiyun was imperial censor, fierce in office; legal officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 瓊推察務在得情，雪者甚眾。

translations.literal: Qiong's investigations aimed at grasping the facts; many were cleared of false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's investigations aimed at facts; many were cleared.

sentences.zh: 寺署台案，始自於瓊。

translations.literal: Temple and ministry case records began with Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and ministry case records began with Qiong.

sentences.zh: 遷三公郎中。

translations.literal: Promoted to gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.

sentences.zh: 趙州及清河、南中有人頻告謀反，前後皆付瓊推檢，事多申雪。

translations.literal: In Zhao Province and in Qinghe and Southern Zhong there were frequent accusations of plotting rebellion; all were handed to Qiong for investigation and many were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhao province and Qinghe and Southern Zhong frequent rebellion accusations were handed to Qiong; many were cleared.

sentences.zh: 尚書崔昂謂瓊曰：「若欲立功名，當更思餘理。

translations.literal: Minister Cui Ang said to Qiong: "If you wish to establish merit and fame, you should think of other principles.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui Ang told Qiong: "If you wish merit and fame, consider other principles.

sentences.zh: 仍數雪反逆，身命何輕？」

translations.literal: Still you repeatedly clear cases of rebellion—how lightly you hold life!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you repeatedly clear rebellion cases—how lightly you hold life!"

sentences.zh: 瓊正色曰：「所雪者冤枉，不放反逆。」

translations.literal: Qiong said sternly: "Those I clear are wronged; I do not release rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong said sternly: "Those I clear were wronged; I do not release rebels."

sentences.zh: 昂大慚。

translations.literal: Ang was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 京師為之語曰：「斷決無疑蘇珍之。」

translations.literal: The capital had a saying: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi."
translations.idiomatic: The capital said: "Judgment without doubt—Su Zhenzhi."

sentences.zh: 皇建中，賜爵安定縣男、徐州行台左丞，行徐州事。

translations.literal: In Huangjian he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anding County, left aide of the Xu Province expeditionary staff, and administered Xu Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangjian he was enfeoffed as baron of Anding county, left aide on the Xu province expeditionary staff, and administered Xu province.

sentences.zh: 徐州城中五級寺忽被盜銅像一百軀。

translations.literal: In Xu province city the Five-Tier Temple was suddenly robbed of a hundred bronze statues.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuzhou city the Five-Tier Temple was robbed of a hundred bronze statues.

sentences.zh: 有司徵檢，四鄰防宿及蹤跡所疑，逮係數十人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices investigated; neighbors on night watch and those suspected by tracks—several tens were seized and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities investigated; neighbors on night watch and those suspicion touched—several tens were seized.

sentences.zh: 瓊一時放遣，寺僧怨訴不為推賊。

translations.literal: Qiong released them all at once; the temple monks complained he was not pursuing the thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong released them all; temple monks complained he was not pursuing the thieves.

sentences.zh: 瓊遣僧，謝曰「但且還寺，得像自送。」

translations.literal: Qiong sent word to the monks, apologizing: "Just return to the temple—the statues will be sent back themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong told the monks: "Return to the temple—the statues will come back on their own."

sentences.zh: 爾後十日，抄賊姓名及贓處所，徑收掩，悉獲實驗。

translations.literal: Ten days later he copied out the thieves' names and where the loot was hidden, went straight to seize them, and obtained full proof.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he identified the thieves and loot, seized them, and proved the case.

sentences.zh: 賊徒款引，道俗歎伏。

translations.literal: The thieves confessed; clerics and laity sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The thieves confessed; clergy and laity marveled.

sentences.zh: 舊制，以淮禁不聽商販輒度。

translations.literal: Old regulations prohibited merchants from crossing the Huai at will.
translations.idiomatic: Old rules forbade merchants to cross the Huai freely.

sentences.zh: 淮南歲儉，啟聽淮北取糴。

translations.literal: That year Huainan had famine; he memorialized to allow buying grain north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Huainan had famine; he allowed grain purchases north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 後淮北人饑，復請通糴淮南，遂得商估往還，彼此兼濟，水陸之利，通于河北。

translations.literal: Later the people north of the Huai were hungry; they again requested passage to buy grain in Huainan; thus merchants went back and forth, each aiding the other; the profit of water and land routes reached Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Later northerners were hungry and trade reopened with Huainan; merchants aided each other and waterways profited Hebei.

sentences.zh: 後為大理卿而齊亡，仕周，為博陵太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as Minister of Justice; when Qi perished he served Zhou as Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as minister of justice; after Qi's fall he served Zhou as prefect of Boling.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初卒。

translations.literal: In the founding of Sui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Sui.

sentences.zh: 路去病，陽平人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qubing was a man of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qubing was a native of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 風神疏朗，儀錶瑰異。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were open and clear; his appearance was singular and striking.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was open and clear; his appearance was striking.

sentences.zh: 齊河清初，為殿中侍御史，彈劾不避貴戚，以正直知名。

translations.literal: In the early Heqing period of Qi he served as palace attendant censor, impeaching without fearing noble kin, famed for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Heqing he served as attendant censor, impeaching without fearing the powerful, famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 敕用士人為縣宰，以去病為定州饒陽縣令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that literati be used as county magistrates; Qubing was made Magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required cultivated men as county magistrates; Qubing was appointed magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 去病明閒時務，性頗嚴毅，人不敢欺，然至廉平，為吏人歎伏。

translations.literal: Qubing was clear and adept in affairs of the time; his nature was rather stern and firm—men did not dare deceive him, yet he was utterly fair and incorrupt, and officials and commoners alike sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing understood affairs of the age and was stern and firm; none dared cheat him, yet he was fair, and officials and people admired him.

sentences.zh: 武平四年，為成安縣令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuping he was Magistrate of Cheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuping he was magistrate of Cheng'an.

sentences.zh: 都下有鄴、臨漳、成安三縣，輦轂之下，舊號難為。

translations.literal: Near the capital lay Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an—three counties long hard to govern under the imperial hub; compounded by chaotic times and slack law, imperial kin made endless requests.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an below the capital were notoriously hard to govern; in chaotic times imperial kin pressed endless requests.

sentences.zh: 重以政亂時艱，綱紀不立，近臣內戚，請屬百端。

translations.literal: Compounded by chaotic government and hard times, the net of law was not established, and meritorious ministers and imperial affines made requests from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Law's net hung slack; meritorious ministers and imperial affines pressed requests from every side.

sentences.zh: 去病消息事宜，以理抗答。

translations.literal: Qubing kept himself informed of affairs and answered with reason.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing tracked affairs and answered on principle.

sentences.zh: 勢要之徒，雖廝養小人，莫不憚其風格，亦不至嫌恨。

translations.literal: Men of power—even grooms and petty servants—all feared his integrity of style, yet none came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of influence—even servants—feared his bearing, yet none resented him.

sentences.zh: 自遷鄴以還，三縣令政術，去病獨為稱首。

translations.literal: From the move to Ye onward, among the three county magistrates' methods of governance, Qubing alone was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Ye, among the three magistrates Qubing alone ranked first.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，重其能官，與濟陰郡守公孫景茂二人不被替代，發詔褒揚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he valued their ability in office—Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao, Administrator of Jiyin, were the two not replaced; an edict was issued to praise and commend them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Wu conquered Qi, Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao of Jiyin were not replaced; an edict praised them.

sentences.zh: 去病後以尉遲迥事。

translations.literal: Later Qubing was implicated in Yuwen Jiong's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qubing was implicated in Yuwen Jiong's affair.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，卒于冀氏縣令。

translations.literal: In the early Daye era of Sui he died while serving as Magistrate of Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he died as magistrate of Jishi.

sentences.zh: 梁彥光，字脩芝，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yanguang, courtesy name Xiuzhi, was a man of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yanguang, styled Xiuzhi, was from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，魏秦、華二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was Inspector of Qin and Hua provinces under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao served under Wei as Inspector of Qin and Hua provinces.

sentences.zh: 父顯，周荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xian was Inspector of Jingzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian was Zhou Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥光少岐嶷，有至性，其父毎謂所親曰：「此兒有風骨，當興吾宗。」

translations.literal: From youth Yanguang was outstanding and had a deeply sincere nature; his father often told intimates, “This child has spirit and bearing and will surely make our lineage flourish.”
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was remarkable from youth and deeply sincere by nature. His father often told those close to him, “This child has spirit and bearing; he will surely raise up our clan.”

sentences.zh: 七歳時，父遇篤疾，醫云「餌五石可愈」。

translations.literal: When he was seven, his father suffered a grave illness, and the physician said, “If he takes five-stone powder, he can recover.”
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven, his father fell gravely ill, and the physician said, “He can recover if he takes five-stone powder.”

sentences.zh: 時求紫石英不得，彥光憂瘁，不知所爲。

translations.literal: At the time they sought purple quartz but could not obtain it; Yanguang was worried and worn, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: They could not obtain the needed purple quartz, and Yanguang was so anxious and worn that he did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 忽於園中見一物，彥光所不識，怪而持歸，即紫石英也。

translations.literal: Suddenly he saw an object in the garden that he did not recognize; finding it strange, he brought it back, and it was purple quartz.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he saw something in the garden that he did not recognize. He found it strange and brought it back; it was purple quartz.

sentences.zh: 親屬咸異之，以爲至孝所感。

translations.literal: His relatives all marveled at it and considered it a response brought about by utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His relatives all marveled and took it as a response to his perfect filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，入學，略涉經史，有規檢，造次必以禮。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong under Wei, he entered school, studied the classics and histories in outline, had discipline and restraint, and even in haste always acted according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wei Datong era, he entered school, read broadly enough in the classics and histories, kept strict standards, and even in haste always observed propriety.

sentences.zh: 解褐秘書郎。

translations.literal: He began official service as Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，遷舍人上士。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication, he was promoted to Senior Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou received the abdication, he was promoted to Senior Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，累遷小馭下大夫。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, through successive promotions he became Lower Grand Master of the Lesser Charioteers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, he rose through successive promotions to Lower Grand Master of the Lesser Charioteers.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning for his mother, and his emaciation from grief exceeded ritual requirements.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, and wasted away from grief beyond what ritual required.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起令視事，帝見其毀甚，嗟歎久之。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and ordered to conduct affairs; when the emperor saw how greatly he was wasted, he sighed over him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to resume duties. Seeing how badly he had wasted away, the emperor sighed over him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 後爲御正下大夫，從帝平齊，以功授開府、陽城縣公。

translations.literal: Later he became Lower Grand Master of Correctors and followed the emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was granted Opening Office and Duke of Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Lower Grand Master of Correctors. He followed the emperor in pacifying Qi and for merit was granted Opening Office and made Duke of Yangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜華州刺史，進封華陰郡公，以陽城公轉封一子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Huazhou and advanced in fief to Duke of Huayin Commandery, while the dukedom of Yangcheng was transferred to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Yanguang was appointed Inspector of Huazhou and promoted to Duke of Huayin Commandery, with his former Yangcheng dukedom transferred to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 後拜柱國、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Pillar of State and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Pillar of State and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬帝崩，不之官。

translations.literal: Because the emperor died at that time, he did not go to the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died just then, so he did not proceed to the post.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，以為岐州刺史，兼領宮監，甚有惠政，嘉禾連理，出於州境。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was made Governor of Qi Province and concurrently director of palace construction; he had excellent benevolent government, and auspicious grain with intertwined stalks appeared in the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Liang was appointed governor of Qi province and palace director; his benevolent rule brought auspicious grain in the province.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其能，下詔褒美，賜粟五百斛、物三百段、禦傘一枚，以厲清正。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his ability, issued an edict of commendation, and bestowed five hundred hu of grain, three hundred bolts of goods, and one imperial parasol to encourage purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, issued commendation, and granted grain, goods, and an imperial parasol to encourage integrity.

sentences.zh: 後轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 彥光前在岐州，其俗頗質，以靜鎮之，合境大安，奏課連最，為天下第一。

translations.literal: Earlier in Qi Province the customs were rather plain; he governed with quiet and the whole region was greatly at peace; his memorials of assessment were repeatedly foremost, ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi province he had governed quietly and ranked first in assessment reports.

sentences.zh: 及居相部，如岐州法。

translations.literal: When he took office in Xiang, he used the same methods as in Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiang he governed as he had in Qi.

sentences.zh: 鄴都雜俗，人多變詐，為之作歌，稱其不能理政。

translations.literal: The mixed customs of Ye were many and deceitful; people made songs saying he could not govern.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's mixed customs bred deceit; people sang that he could not govern.

sentences.zh: 上聞而譴之，竟坐免。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and reproached him; in the end he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and rebuked him; he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜趙州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Governor of Zhao Province.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was appointed governor of Zhao province.

sentences.zh: 彥光曰：「臣前待罪相州，百姓呼為戴帽餳。

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "Your servant formerly served at fault in Xiang Province; the people called me 'topped pastry.'
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said: "When I served in Xiang, people called me 'topped pastry.'

sentences.zh: 臣自分廢黜，無復衣冠之望。

translations.literal: Your servant considered myself dismissed and had no further hope of office.
translations.idiomatic: I thought myself finished and without hope of office.

sentences.zh: 不謂天恩復垂收采。

translations.literal: I did not expect Heaven's grace again to gather me in.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect to be recalled.

sentences.zh: 請復為相州，改弦易調，庶有以變其風俗。」

translations.literal: I beg to return to Xiang Province and change the tune and adjust the strings, hoping thereby to transform its customs."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to return to Xiang and change my methods to transform its customs."

sentences.zh: 上從之，復為相州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor assented and again made him Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and reappointed him to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 豪猾者聞彥光自請來，莫不嗤笑。

translations.literal: The powerful and crafty heard Yanguang had asked to come himself and all sneered.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful sneered when they heard he had asked to return.

sentences.zh: 彥光下車，發摘奸隱，有若神明，狡猾莫不潛竄，合境大駭。

translations.literal: When Yanguang took office he exposed and plucked out hidden wickedness like a spirit; the crafty all fled in secret and the whole region was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he exposed hidden crime like a spirit; the crafty fled and the region was stunned.

sentences.zh: 初，齊亡後，衣冠士人，多遷關內，唯技巧商販及樂戶之家，移實州郭。

translations.literal: At first, after Qi's fall, gentry and scholars mostly moved within the Pass; only artisans, merchants, and households of musicians moved into the prefectural cities.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's fall, gentry moved within the Pass; only artisans, merchants, and musicians filled the cities.

sentences.zh: 由是人情險詖，妄起風謠，訴訟官人，萬端千變。

translations.literal: Hence human feelings were treacherous; false rumors arose; lawsuits against officials multiplied endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Feelings grew treacherous; rumors and lawsuits multiplied.

sentences.zh: 彥光欲革其弊，乃用秩俸之物，招致山東大儒，每鄉立學，非聖哲之書不得教授。

translations.literal: Yanguang wished to reform these abuses; he used his salary goods to summon great Confucians from east of the mountains, established schools in each district, and forbade teaching books that were not of sages.
translations.idiomatic: He used his salary to summon great scholars, establish district schools, and forbid unorthodox texts.

sentences.zh: 常以季月召集之，親臨策試。

translations.literal: He regularly summoned them in the seasonal months and personally conducted examination by policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Each season he examined students personally.

sentences.zh: 有勤學異等，聰令有聞者，升堂設饌，其餘並坐廊下。

translations.literal: Those who studied diligently with unusual ability and whose clever orders were heard of—he set a feast in the hall; the rest all sat beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: The excellent dined in the hall; the rest sat in the corridor.

sentences.zh: 有好諍訟惰業無成者，坐之庭中，設以草具。

translations.literal: Those who loved litigation and quarreling but were idle in study and achieved nothing—he seated them in the courtyard with grass mats.
translations.idiomatic: Quarrelsome idlers sat in the courtyard on grass mats.

sentences.zh: 及大成當舉，行賓貢之禮；

translations.literal: When they completed their studies and were to be recommended, he performed the guest-and-tribute rites;
translations.idiomatic: At graduation he performed guest-and-tribute rites;

sentences.zh: 又于郊外祖道，並以財物資之。

translations.literal: he also saw them off at the suburban road and supplied them with goods.
translations.idiomatic: and sent them off with gifts.

sentences.zh: 於是人皆克勵，風俗大改。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were stimulated to effort and customs greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: All were stirred to effort and customs changed greatly.

sentences.zh: 有滏陽人焦通，性酗酒，事親禮闕，為從弟所訟。

translations.literal: There was Jiao Tong of Fuyang, by nature addicted to wine, lacking in filial rites toward parents, sued by his younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Tong of Fuyang drank excessively and neglected his parents; a cousin sued him.

sentences.zh: 彥光弗之罪，將至州學，令觀孔子廟中韓伯瑜母杖不痛，哀母力衰，對母悲泣之像。

translations.literal: Yanguang did not punish him but brought him to the provincial school and had him view the image in Confucius's temple of Han Boyu, whose mother beat him without pain, grieving his mother's weakened strength and weeping before his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang brought him to the school to view the image of Han Boyu weeping before his mother.

sentences.zh: 通遂感悟，悲愧若無容者。

translations.literal: Tong thereupon was moved to awareness and grieved as if he had no place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was moved to shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 彥光訓喻而遣之，後改過勵行，卒為善士。

translations.literal: Yanguang instructed and released him; later he reformed his faults and strove in conduct, and in the end became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang instructed and released him; he reformed and became a good man.

sentences.zh: 吏人感悅，略無諍訟。

translations.literal: Officials and people were moved and pleased; litigation and quarreling nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people rejoiced; lawsuits nearly ceased.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈冀定瀛青四州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Ji, Ding, Ying, and Qing Provinces, posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumously enfeoffed over four provinces, posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子文謙嗣，弘雅有父風。

translations.literal: His son Wenqian succeeded, refined and elegant with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenqian succeeded him, refined like his father.

sentences.zh: 以上柱國世子，例授儀同。

translations.literal: As son of a supreme pillar of state, by precedent he was appointed Palace Guard of the Fifth Order.
translations.idiomatic: As a pillar's son he was appointed palace guard of the fifth order.

sentences.zh: 曆上、饒二州刺史，遷鄱陽太守，稱為天下之最。

translations.literal: He served successively as Governor of Shang and Rao and as Administrator of Poyang, called the foremost in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Shang and Rao and prefect of Poyang, called foremost in the realm.

sentences.zh: 徵拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，領武賁郎將，為盧龍道軍副。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he led Martial Guard General and served as deputy on the Lulong route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he led martial guard troops as deputy on the Lulong route.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，其弟武賁郎將玄縱先隸文謙，玄感反問未至而玄縱逃走，文謙不之覺。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his younger brother Martial Guard General Xuanzong had first been under Wenqian's command; before news of the rebellion arrived Xuanzong fled; Wenqian did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his brother Xuanzong fled before news arrived; Wenqian did not notice.

sentences.zh: 坐是，配防桂林而卒。

translations.literal: For this he was sentenced to guard Guilin and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to guard Guilin and died there.

sentences.zh: 少子文讓，初封陽城縣公，後爲鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: The younger son Wenrang was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng county and later served as Soaring Hawk General.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Wenrang was first enfeoffed as Duke of Yangcheng and later served as Soaring Hawk General.

sentences.zh: 從衞玄擊楊玄感於東都，力戰而死，贈通議大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Wei Xuan in attacking Yang Xuangan at the Eastern Capital, fought fiercely and died, and was posthumously granted Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Wei Xuan in the attack on Yang Xuangan at the Eastern Capital, fought fiercely until he was killed, and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 樊叔略，陳留人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shulüe was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shulüe was a native of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父觀，仕魏，為南兗州刺史、河陽侯，為高氏所誅。

translations.literal: His father Guan served Wei as Governor of Southern Yanzhou and Marquis of Heyang; he was executed by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guan served Wei and was executed by the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 叔略被腐刑，給使殿省。

translations.literal: Shulüe suffered castration and was made an attendant in the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Shulüe was castrated and served in the palace.

sentences.zh: 身長九尺，有志氣。

translations.literal: He was nine chi tall and had ambition and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chi tall, he was ambitious and spirited.

sentences.zh: 頗見忌，內不自安，遂奔關西。

translations.literal: He was much envied, felt insecure within, and fled to the west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Envied and insecure, he fled west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 周文器之，引置左右，授都督，襲爵為侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued him, brought him to his side, appointed him Commander, and he inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued him, made him commander, and he inherited a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護執政，引為中尉。

translations.literal: When Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, he was made chief jailer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu held power, he was made chief jailer.

sentences.zh: 漸被委信，兼督內外，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Gradually trusted, he oversaw inner and outer affairs, rank Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually trusted, he oversaw inner and outer affairs at opening-office rank.

sentences.zh: 護誅，齊王憲引為園苑監。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Prince Xian of Qi made him director of the imperial parks.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was killed, Prince Xian made him parks director.

sentences.zh: 數進兵謀，憲甚奇之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly offered military stratagems; Xian greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He offered military plans; Xian marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，以功加上開府，封清鄉縣公，拜汴州刺史，號為明決。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, for merit he was advanced to Upper Opening Office, enfeoffed Duke of Qingxiang, appointed Administrator of Bianzhou, and called Clear Decider.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu against Qi, he rose to upper opening office, was enfeoffed duke of Qingxiang, and made prefect of Bianzhou, called Clear Decider.

sentences.zh: 宣帝營建東都，以叔略有巧思，拜營構監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan built the eastern capital, because Shulüe had clever thought he was made director of construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan built the eastern capital, Shulüe was made construction director.

sentences.zh: 宮室制度，皆叔略所定。

translations.literal: The palace regulations were all set by Shulüe.
translations.idiomatic: Palace regulations were all his work.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥之亂，鎮大梁，以軍功拜大將軍，復為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yuwen Jiong's rebellion he guarded Daliang; for military merit he was made Grand General and again Administrator of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuwen Jiong's rebellion he guarded Daliang and was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，加位上大將軍，進爵安定郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was advanced to Upper Grand General and promoted to Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne, he was advanced to upper grand general and duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: Several years in the province he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Years in office won great reputation.

sentences.zh: 遷相州刺史，政為當時第一。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Xiang Province, his government was first in the age.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Xiang his government ranked first.

sentences.zh: 上降璽書褒美之，賜以粟帛，班示天下。

translations.literal: The emperor sent down a sealed edict praising him, bestowing grain and silks, and proclaiming it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him by edict and bestowed grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之語曰：「智無窮，清鄉公；

translations.literal: The people made a saying: "Wisdom without end, Duke of Qingxiang;
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Wisdom without end—the Duke of Qingxiang;

sentences.zh: 上下正，樊安定。」

translations.literal: upright above and below, Fan of Anding."
translations.idiomatic: upright above and below—Fan of Anding."

sentences.zh: 徵拜司農卿，吏人莫不流涕，相與立碑頌德。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Agriculture; officials and people all wept and together erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as minister of agriculture, people wept and erected a praising stele.

sentences.zh: 自為司農，凡所種植，叔略別有條制，皆出人意表。

translations.literal: From the time he was Minister of Agriculture, all planting he regulated had special rules, all beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of agriculture, all planting followed his unexpected rules.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有疑滯，公卿所未能決，叔略輒為評理。

translations.literal: When the court had knotty problems the excellencies could not resolve, Shulüe would judge and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had problems excellencies could not solve, Shulüe judged them.

sentences.zh: 雖無學術，有所依據，然師心獨見，暗與理合。

translations.literal: Though without learning, he had grounds to rely on; yet following his own mind alone, he darkly accorded with principle.
translations.idiomatic: Without formal learning, he yet darkly matched principle.

sentences.zh: 甚為上所親委，高熲、楊素禮遇之。

translations.literal: He was greatly trusted by the emperor; Gao Jiong and Yang Su treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him; Gao Jiong and Yang Su honored him.

sentences.zh: 叔略雖為司農，往往參督九卿事。

translations.literal: Though Shulüe was Minister of Agriculture, he often oversaw the affairs of the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Though minister of agriculture, he often oversaw nine-minister affairs.

sentences.zh: 性頗豪侈，每食方丈，備水陸。

translations.literal: By nature he was rather extravagant; each meal filled a square zhang with land and water delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant by nature, each meal was lavish.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從祠太山。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the sacrifice at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he attended the Mount Tai sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，上令錄囚徒。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, the emperor ordered him to record prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang the emperor ordered him to record prisoners.

sentences.zh: 將奏，晨至獄門，於馬上暴卒，上嗟悼久之。

translations.literal: About to memorialize, in the morning he reached the prison gate and suddenly died on his horse; the emperor sighed and mourned long.
translations.idiomatic: About to report, he died suddenly at the prison gate; the emperor mourned long.

sentences.zh: 贈亳州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Bo Province, posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed as governor of Bo, posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 公孫景茂，字元蔚，河間阜城人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Jingmao, styled Yuanwei, was a man of Fucheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Jingmao, courtesy name Yuanwei, was a native of Fucheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁梧，少好學，博涉經史。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing; in youth he loved learning and broadly traversed the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing, in youth he loved learning and read widely in the classics.

sentences.zh: 在魏，察孝廉，射策甲科。

translations.literal: In Wei he was examined as Filial and Incorrupt and in archery examination ranked first class.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and ranked first in the archery examination.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太常博士，多所損益，時人稱為書庫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, making many improvements; people of the time called him a library of books.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to doctor of the grand sacrifices, he made many improvements; contemporaries called him a walking library.

sentences.zh: 曆高唐令、大理正，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as Magistrate of Gaotang and Director of Justice, both with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Gaotang and director of justice, famed for ability in both.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，周武帝聞而召見，與語器之，授濟北太守。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard and summoned him, spoke with him and valued his capacity, and appointed him Administrator of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's fall, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him, valued his talent, and made him prefect of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，召拜汝南太守。

translations.literal: In the founding of Kaihuang he was summoned and appointed Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was appointed prefect of Runan.

sentences.zh: 郡廢，為曹州司馬，遷息州刺史。

translations.literal: When the commandery was abolished he became Marshal of Cao Province and was transferred to Governor of Xi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was abolished he became Cao province marshal, then governor of Xi.

sentences.zh: 法令清靜，德化大行。

translations.literal: Laws and orders were pure and quiet; transforming virtue was greatly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were quiet; moral transformation flourished.

sentences.zh: 屬平陳之役，征人在路病者，景茂減俸祿為饘粥湯藥，多方振濟之，賴全活者千數。

translations.literal: During the campaign to pacify Chen, conscripts on the road who fell ill—Jingmao reduced his salary to provide gruel, soup, and medicine and in many ways relieved them; those who lived thanks to this numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chen campaign he used his salary for gruel, medicine, and relief for sick conscripts, saving thousands.

sentences.zh: 上聞嘉之，詔宣示天下。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended this; an edict proclaimed it to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上幸洛陽，景茂謁見。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang; Jingmao had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang and received Jingmao.

sentences.zh: 時七十七，上命升殿坐。

translations.literal: He was then seventy-seven; the emperor ordered him to ascend the hall and be seated.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-seven he was seated in the hall by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 問其年，哀其老，嗟歎久之。

translations.literal: Asked his age, the emperor pitied his old age and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his age, the emperor pitied his age and sighed long.

sentences.zh: 景茂再拜曰：「呂望八十而遇文王，臣逾七十而逢陛下。」

translations.literal: Jingmao bowed again and said: "Lü Wang met King Wen at eighty; your servant passes seventy and meets Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao said: "Lü Wang met King Wen at eighty; I pass seventy and meet Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，下詔褒美之，加上儀同三司，伊州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased, issued an edict praising him, and advanced him to Upper Palace Guard of the Third Order and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, advanced him to upper palace guard of the third order, and made him governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 明年，以疾征，吏人號泣於道。

translations.literal: The next year, recalled for illness, officials and people wailed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled for illness, officials and people wailed along the road.

sentences.zh: 及疾愈，復乞骸骨，又不許。

translations.literal: When his illness healed he again begged to retire; again it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When healed he begged to retire again; again refused.

sentences.zh: 轉道州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Dao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Dao province.

sentences.zh: 悉以秩俸買牛犢雞豬，散惠孤弱不自存者。

translations.literal: He used all his salary to buy oxen, calves, chickens, and pigs and distributed them to the orphaned and weak who could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his salary on livestock and gave them to orphans and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 好單騎巡人，家至戶入，閱視百姓產業。

translations.literal: He liked to patrol alone on horseback, entering every home, inspecting the people's livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He patrolled alone, entering homes to inspect livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 有修理者，于都會時，乃褒揚稱述；

translations.literal: Those who had improved their affairs—at the time of the great assembly he praised and proclaimed them;
translations.idiomatic: Those who improved their affairs he praised at the great assembly;

sentences.zh: 如有過惡，隨即訓導，而不彰也。

translations.literal: if there were faults and evils, he immediately instructed and guided without exposing them.
translations.idiomatic: those at fault he guided privately without exposing them.

sentences.zh: 由是人行義讓，有無均通。

translations.literal: Hence people practiced righteousness and yielding; having or lacking was mutually shared.
translations.idiomatic: People practiced righteousness; resources were shared.

sentences.zh: 男子相助耕耘，婦女相從紡織，大村或數百戶，皆如一家之務。

translations.literal: Men helped one another in plowing; women followed one another in spinning; large villages of several hundred households all worked like one family.
translations.idiomatic: Men helped plow; women spun together; large villages worked as one family.

sentences.zh: 其後請致仕，上優詔聽之。

translations.literal: Later he requested retirement; the emperor graciously assented by edict.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on an gracious imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，上明公楊紀出使河北，見景茂神力不衰，還以狀奏。

translations.literal: In Renshou, Duke Yang Ji of Shangming went on mission to Hebei, saw Jingmao's strength had not declined, and on return memorialized the fact.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou Duke Yang Ji saw Jingmao's vigor undiminished and reported it.

sentences.zh: 於是就拜淄州刺史，賜以馬輦，便道之官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed on the spot Governor of Zi Province, granted a carriage, and went to office by expedited route.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Zi, granted a carriage, and sent directly to office.

sentences.zh: 前後曆職，皆有德政，論者稱為良牧。

translations.literal: In every office before and after he had virtuous government; discussants called him a good shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: Every post showed virtuous rule; critics called him a good shepherd.

sentences.zh: 大業初，卒官。

translations.literal: In the early Daye period he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he died in office.

sentences.zh: 年八十七，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Age eighty-seven; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-seven; posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 身死之日，諸州人吏赴喪者數千人。

translations.literal: On the day of his death several thousand officials and people from the provinces came to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands came to his funeral.

sentences.zh: 或不及葬，皆望墳慟哭，野祭而去。

translations.literal: Some could not reach the burial; all gazed at the mound and wailed, making wild sacrifices and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Some could not attend burial; mourners wailed at his mound and left wild offerings.

sentences.zh: 辛公義，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Gongyi was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongyi was from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 祖徽，魏徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Wei Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was Wei Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父季慶，青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jiqing was Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiqing was Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 公義早孤，爲母氏所養，親授《書》、《傳》。

translations.literal: Gongyi was orphaned early and was raised by his mother’s family; they personally taught him the Documents and the Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi was orphaned young and raised by his mother’s family, who personally taught him the Documents and the commentaries.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，選良家子任太學生。

translations.literal: During the Tianhe era of Zhou, he was selected as a son of a good family to serve as an Imperial University student.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou Tianhe era, he was selected from the sons of respectable families to become a student at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，召入露門學，令受道義，毎月集御前，令與大儒講論。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, he was summoned into the Lumen School and ordered to receive instruction in principles and right conduct; each month he assembled before the emperor and was ordered to debate with great scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, he was summoned to the Lumen School to study moral principles. Each month he assembled before the emperor and debated with great scholars.

sentences.zh: 上數嗟異，時輩慕之。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sighed in admiration, and his contemporaries admired him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sighed in admiration, and his contemporaries looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 建德初，授宣納中士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Middle Clerk of Proclamation and Reception.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Middle Clerk of Proclamation and Reception.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，累遷掌治上士、掃寇將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Qi, and through successive promotions became Senior Clerk in Charge of Administration and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Qi and rose through successive promotions to Senior Clerk in Charge of Administration and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，授內史上士，參掌機要。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as chief minister, Gongyi was appointed Senior Clerk of the Secretariat and participated in handling confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Gongyi was appointed Senior Clerk of the Secretariat and helped manage confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，除主客侍郎，攝內史舍人，賜爵安陽縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Gentleman Attendant of Guests, acted as Secretariat Drafter, and was granted the title Baron of Anyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In 581, he was appointed Gentleman Attendant of Guests, acted as Secretariat Drafter, and was granted the title Baron of Anyang County.

sentences.zh: 轉駕部侍郎，使勾檢諸馬牧，所獲十餘萬匹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Chariot Bureau and sent to inspect the horse pastures, where he obtained more than a hundred thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Chariot Bureau and sent to audit the horse pastures, recovering more than a hundred thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「唯我公義，奉國罄心。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said, “Only my Gongyi serves the state with all his heart.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, “Only my Gongyi devotes his whole heart to serving the state.”

sentences.zh: 從軍平陳，以功除岷州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the army in pacifying Chen, for merit he was made Governor of Min Province.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in pacifying Chen he was made governor of Min province.

sentences.zh: 土俗畏病，若一人有疾，即闔家避之，父子夫妻，不相看養，孝義道絕。

translations.literal: The local custom feared illness; if one person fell ill the whole family fled; father and son, husband and wife, did not care for one another—filial duty was severed.
translations.idiomatic: Locals fled illness; families abandoned the sick and filial bonds broke.

sentences.zh: 由是病者多死。

translations.literal: Hence many of the ill died.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the sick died.

sentences.zh: 公義患之，欲變其俗。

translations.literal: Gongyi was distressed and wished to change the custom.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi wished to change the custom.

sentences.zh: 因分遣官人，巡檢部內，凡有疾病，皆以床輦來，安置査事。

translations.literal: He therefore sent out officials to patrol within the prefecture; wherever there was illness they were brought on beds and litters to the investigation hall.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officials to bring the sick to the hall on litters.

sentences.zh: 暑月疫時，病人或至數百，査廊悉滿。

translations.literal: In the hot months of epidemic, the sick sometimes reached several hundred; the corridors of the hall were all full.
translations.idiomatic: In epidemics hundreds filled the hall corridors.

sentences.zh: 公義親設一榻，獨坐其間，終日連夕，對之理事。

translations.literal: Gongyi personally set one couch and sat alone among them from day through night, handling affairs facing them.
translations.idiomatic: He sat alone among them day and night handling cases.

sentences.zh: 所得秩俸，盡用市藥，迎醫療之，躬勸其飲食，於是悉差。

translations.literal: All his salary he used to buy medicine, summon doctors to treat them, and personally urge their food and drink; thereby all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his salary on medicine and doctors until all recovered.

sentences.zh: 方召其親戚而喻之曰：「死生由命，不關相著，前汝棄之，所以死耳。

translations.literal: Then he summoned their kin and instructed them: "Life and death are by fate, not related to contact; formerly you abandoned them, hence they died.
translations.idiomatic: He told kin: "Life and death are fate; you abandoned the sick, so they died.

sentences.zh: 今我聚病者，坐臥其間，若言相染，那得不死？

translations.literal: Now I gather the sick and sit among them; if contact spread disease, how would they not die?
translations.idiomatic: Now I sit among them; if contact killed, how would any live?

sentences.zh: 病兒復差，汝等勿復信之。」

translations.literal: The sick children recovered; you must no longer believe this."
translations.idiomatic: The sick recovered—do not believe this again."

sentences.zh: 諸病家子孫，慚謝而去。

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons of the sick families bowed in shame and left.
translations.idiomatic: Families bowed in shame and left.

sentences.zh: 後人有過疾者，爭就使君，其家親屬，固留養之。

translations.literal: Later when people fell ill they vied to go to the governor; their families and kin firmly kept them to be cared for.
translations.idiomatic: Later the sick sought the governor; families kept them to be cared for.

sentences.zh: 始相慈愛，此風遂革，合境之內，呼為慈母。

translations.literal: They began to love one another; this custom was reformed; within the whole region he was called Motherly Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Love returned; the custom changed; he was called Motherly Governor.

sentences.zh: 後遷并州刺史。

translations.literal: Later transferred to Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later governor of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 下車，先至獄中，因露坐牢側，親自驗問。

translations.literal: On taking office he first went to the prison, exposed the jail and sat beside it, personally examining and questioning.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he first examined prisoners personally.

sentences.zh: 十餘日間，決斷咸盡。

translations.literal: Within ten-odd days judgments were all completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days all cases were decided.

sentences.zh: 方還大査，受領新訟。

translations.literal: Then he returned to the main hall and received new lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Then he returned to the main hall for new suits.

sentences.zh: 皆不立文案，遣當直佐僚一人，側坐訊問。

translations.literal: He kept no documents; he sent one on-duty aide to sit at the side and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no files; one aide inquired at his side.

sentences.zh: 事若不盡，應須禁者，公義即宿査事，終不還閣。

translations.literal: If matters were not finished and detention was needed, Gongyi lodged in the hall and never returned to his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: If detention was needed he lodged in the hall and never returned to quarters.

sentences.zh: 人或諫之曰：「此事有程，使君何自苦也？」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him: "This matter has its schedule—why torment yourself, Governor?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "This has a schedule—why torment yourself?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「刺史無德可以導人，尚令百姓系于囹圄。

translations.literal: He answered: "A governor without virtue to guide people still has the people bound in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Without virtue to guide people, I still bind them in prison.

sentences.zh: 豈有禁人在獄，而心自安乎！」

translations.literal: How can one detain people in prison while the heart is at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: How can my heart be at ease while they are jailed!"

sentences.zh: 罪人聞之，咸自款服。

translations.literal: The criminals heard and all confessed willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals heard and confessed willingly.

sentences.zh: 後有欲諍訟者，鄉閭父老遽相曉曰：「此蓋小事，何忍勤勞使君！」

translations.literal: Later those who wished to litigate—elders of the villages quickly told one another: "This is a small matter—how can we bear to trouble the Governor!"
translations.idiomatic: Elders said: "This is small—do not trouble the governor!"

sentences.zh: 訟者多兩讓而止。

translations.literal: Most litigants yielded twice and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Most suits ended in mutual yielding.

sentences.zh: 時山東霖雨，自陳汝至於滄海，皆苦水災。

translations.literal: At that time in Shandong there was continuous rain; from Chen and Ru to the sea all suffered flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck Shandong from Chen and Ru to the sea.

sentences.zh: 境內犬牙，獨無所損。

translations.literal: Within his borders alone there was no damage.
translations.idiomatic: His borders alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 山出黃銀，獲之以獻，詔水部郎婁崱就公義禱焉，乃聞空中有金石絲竹之響。

translations.literal: The mountains produced yellow silver; he obtained it and presented it; an edict sent Master of Waterworks Lou Kai to pray at Gongyi's place, and there was heard in the air the sound of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow silver from the mountains was offered; prayers brought sounds of music in the air.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，追充揚州道黜陟大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, he was additionally appointed Grand Commissioner for Demotion and Promotion on the Yangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 601, he was additionally appointed Grand Commissioner for reviewing officials on the Yangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 豫章王暕恐其部內官僚犯法，未入州境，豫令使屬之。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Yuzhang feared that officials within his jurisdiction had violated the law, and before Gongyi entered the province’s territory, he first sent an envoy to entrust matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Yuzhang feared that officials under him had broken the law, so before Gongyi entered the province, he sent an envoy ahead to make a private appeal.

sentences.zh: 公義答曰：「不敢有私。」

translations.literal: Gongyi replied, “I do not dare to have private considerations.”
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi replied, “I would not dare show private favor.”

sentences.zh: 及至揚州，皆無所縱舍，暕銜之。

translations.literal: When he reached Yangzhou, he did not indulge or spare anyone, and Jian resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongyi reached Yangzhou, he indulged and spared no one, and Jian bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，揚州長史王弘入爲黃門郎，因言公義之短，竟去官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Wang Hong, Chief Administrator of Yangzhou, entered court as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then spoke of Gongyi’s shortcomings, so Gongyi was ultimately removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang took the throne, Wang Hong, Chief Administrator of Yangzhou, entered court as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and used the occasion to speak against Gongyi; in the end Gongyi was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 吏人守闕訴冤，相繼不絶。

translations.literal: Officials and people waited at the palace gate to complain of the injustice, one after another without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners waited at the palace gate to plead against the injustice, continuing one after another without interruption.

sentences.zh: 後數歳，帝悟，除內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Several years later, the emperor realized the truth and appointed him Secretariat Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, the emperor understood the matter and appointed Gongyi Secretariat Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，未幾起爲司隸大夫，檢校右御衞武賁郎將。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; before long he was recalled as Grand Master of the Metropolitan Commandant and acting Martial Guard General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother, but before long was recalled as Grand Master of the Metropolitan Commandant and acting Martial Guard General of the Right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 從徵至柳城郡，卒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to Liucheng Commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign as far as Liucheng Commandery and died there.

sentences.zh: 子融。

translations.literal: His son was Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rong.

sentences.zh: 柳儉，字道約，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, styled Daoyue, was a man of Hedong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, courtesy name Daoyue, was from Hedong Jie.

sentences.zh: 祖元璋，魏司州大中正、相、華二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanzhang was Wei Chief Rectifier of Si Province and Governor of Xiang and Hua Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanzhang was Wei chief rectifier of Si and governor of Xiang and Hua.

sentences.zh: 父裕，周聞喜令。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Magistrate of Wenxi under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was magistrate of Wenxi under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 儉有局量，立行清苦，為州裏所敬，雖至親昵，無敢狎侮。

translations.literal: Jian had breadth of measure; his conduct was pure and hard; the province respected him—even close kin did not dare be familiar or insulting.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was measured and austere; even kin did not treat him lightly.

sentences.zh: 仕周，曆宣納上士、畿伯大夫。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he rose through Attendant of the Secretariat of the Upper Rank and Grandee of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he rose through secretariat and capital grandee ranks.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝受禪，擢拜水部侍郎，封率道縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was promoted to Vice Minister of Waterworks and enfeoffed Baron of Shuaidao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne he became vice minister of waterworks and baron of Shuaidao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為廣漢太守，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Administrator of Guanghan, with a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Soon prefect of Guanghan, famed for ability.

sentences.zh: 俄而郡廢。

translations.literal: Soon the commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 時帝勵精思政，妙簡良能，出為牧宰。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor strove in government and carefully selected the able, sending them out as shepherds and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor selected the able for provincial office.

sentences.zh: 儉以仁明著稱，擢拜蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian was famed for benevolence and clarity and was promoted to Governor of Peng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Famed for benevolence, he was made governor of Peng.

sentences.zh: 獄訟者庭決遣之，佐吏從容而已，獄無系囚。

translations.literal: Litigants were decided in the courtyard and dismissed; aides were at ease; the prison had no detained prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He decided suits in court; the prison held no detainees.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀時鎮益州，列上其事。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiu of Shu then held Yizhou he reported this upward.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu reported this upward.

sentences.zh: 遷邛州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Qiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Qiong.

sentences.zh: 在職十餘年，人夷悅服。

translations.literal: More than ten years in office; Chinese and barbarians were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in office; Chinese and barbarians submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之得罪也，儉坐與交通，免職。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiu of Shu was condemned, Jian was implicated for communication and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu fell, Jian was dismissed for association.

sentences.zh: 及還鄉，妻子衣食不贍，見者咸歎伏焉。

translations.literal: On returning home his wife and children lacked food and clothing; viewers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home poor, onlookers admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang succeeded he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 于時，多以功臣任職，牧州領郡者，並帶戎資，唯儉起自良吏。

translations.literal: At that time many meritorious ministers held office; those who were shepherds and led commanderies all bore military qualifications—only Jian rose from a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Many meritorious men held office with military titles—only Jian rose as a civil magistrate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其績，特授朝散大夫，拜弘化太守，儉清節愈勵。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his achievements, specially appointed him Palace Scattered Grandee, and made him Administrator of Honghua; Jian's pure integrity was further strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, made him scattered grandee and prefect of Honghua.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，入朝，郡國畢集。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he entered court; commanderies and states all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year five he came to court as commanderies gathered.

sentences.zh: 帝謂納言蘇威、吏部尚書牛弘曰：「其中清名天下第一者，為誰？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Master of Documents Su Wei and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong: "Among them, who has the foremost pure name in the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei and Hong, "Among them, who has the purest name in the realm?"

sentences.zh: 威等以儉對。

translations.literal: Wei and others answered with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: They named Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝又問其次，威以涿郡贊務郭絢，潁川贊務敬肅等二人對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who was next; Wei named Guo Xuan, assistant of Zhuo Commandery, and Jing Su, assistant of Yingchuan, among the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Next he named Guo Xuan of Zhuo and Jing Su of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 帝賜儉帛二百匹，絢、肅各一百匹，令天下朝集使送至郡邸，以旌異焉，論者美之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Jian two hundred bolts of silk, on Xuan and Su one hundred each, and ordered envoys from the realm's assemblies to deliver them to the commandery lodges to mark distinction; discussants praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian received two hundred bolts of silk; Xuan and Su one hundred each; critics praised the honor.

sentences.zh: 及大業末，盜賊峰起，數被攻逼。

translations.literal: By the end of Daye bandits rose everywhere and he was repeatedly attacked and pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye bandits repeatedly attacked.

sentences.zh: 儉撫結人夷，卒無離叛，竟以保全。

translations.literal: Jian soothed and bound Chinese and barbarians; in the end none rebelled and he was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed all peoples; none rebelled; he was preserved.

sentences.zh: 及義兵至長安，尊立恭帝，儉與留守李粲縞素，于州南向慟哭。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Chang'an and honored the Gong Emperor, Jian with the garrison commander Li Can wore white mourning and wailed facing south in the province.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army installed Gongdi, Jian and Li Can mourned in white facing south.

sentences.zh: 既而歸京師，相國賜儉物三百段，就拜上大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon returning to the capital, the chief minister bestowed three hundred bolts of goods on Jian and appointed him Upper Grand General on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, the chief minister honored him and made him upper grand general.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒于家，時年八十九。

translations.literal: After a year he died at home, age eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at home, aged eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 郭絢，河東安邑人，家世寒微。

translations.literal: Guo Xuan was a man of Anyi in Hedong; his family for generations was humble and slight.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xuan was from Anyi in Hedong, of humble family.

sentences.zh: 初為尚書令史，後以軍功拜儀同，歷數州司馬、長史，皆有能名。

translations.literal: At first he was a clerk in the Secretariat of the Master of Documents; later for military merit he was made Palace Guard of the Same Order, and served successively as marshal and chief administrator of several provinces—all with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from secretariat clerk to palace guard through military merit, serving ably in several provinces.

sentences.zh: 大業初，刑部尚書宇文幹巡省河北，引絢為副。

translations.literal: In the early Daye period Minister of Justice Yuwen Gan toured Hebei and took Xuan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye Yuwen Gan took him as deputy on a Hebei tour.

sentences.zh: 煬帝將有事遼東，以涿郡為沖要，訪可任者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was about to campaign in Liaodong, Zhuo Commandery was critical; he sought who could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: For the Liaodong campaign he sought who could hold Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 聞絢有幹局，拜涿郡贊務，吏人悅服。

translations.literal: Hearing Xuan had capacity and plan, he was made Assistant of Zhuo Commandery; officials and people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was made Zhuo assistant; officials and people approved.

sentences.zh: 數載，遷為通守，兼領留守。

translations.literal: After several years he was promoted to Governor and concurrently garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: After years he became governor and garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 及山東盜起，絢逐捕之，多所克獲。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shandong, Xuan pursued and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: He captured many Shandong bandits.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡無復完者，唯涿郡獨全。

translations.literal: At the time no commandery remained intact; only Zhuo was whole.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhuo remained intact.

sentences.zh: 後將兵擊竇建德於河間，戰死，人吏哭之，數月不息。

translations.literal: Later leading troops he attacked Dou Jiande at Hejian and died in battle; officials and people wept for months without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting Dou Jiande at Hejian; mourning lasted months.

sentences.zh: 敬肅，字敬儉，河東蒲阪人。

translations.literal: Jing Su, styled Jingjian, was a man of Puzhou in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Su, courtesy name Jingjian, was from Puzhou in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少以貞介知名，釋褐州主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for upright integrity; upon doffing the hemp he became a provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was famed for integrity; he began as a provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為安陵令，有能名。

translations.literal: In the founding of Kaihuang he was Magistrate of Anling, with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was magistrate of Anling, famed for ability.

sentences.zh: 擢拜秦州司馬，轉幽州長史。

translations.literal: Promoted to Marshal of Qin Province, transferred to Chief Administrator of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Qin marshal, then chief administrator of You.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，為衛州司馬，俱有異績。

translations.literal: In Renshou he was Marshal of Wei Province; both had outstanding records.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou he was Wei marshal with outstanding records.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，遷潁川郡贊務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was transferred to Assistant of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang succeeded he was Yingchuan assistant.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，朝東都。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he had audience at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year five he attended court at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 帝令司隸大夫薛道衡為天下郡官之狀，稱肅曰：「心如鐵石，老而彌篤。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Master of Corrections Xue Daoheng to compose evaluations of commandery officials throughout the realm, praising Su: "His heart is like iron and stone, firmer in old age."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng's evaluations praised Su: "His heart is iron and stone, firmer with age."

sentences.zh: 時左翊衛大將軍宇文述當塗用事，其邑在潁州，每有書屬肅，肅未嘗開封，輒令使者持去。

translations.literal: At that time Left Wing Guard General Yuwen Shu held power; his home district was in Yingzhou; whenever he sent letters entrusting Su, Su never opened the seal but had the messenger take them away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu often sent letters; Su never opened them but returned them unopened.

sentences.zh: 述賓客有放縱者，以法繩之，無所寬貸，由是述銜之。

translations.literal: Shu's guests who were unrestrained—he bound them by law without leniency; hence Shu bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: He punished Shu's unruly guests by law; Shu resented him.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝於涿郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he had audience at Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he attended at Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 帝以其年老，有能名，將擢為太守者數矣，輒為述所毀，不行。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was old and had a reputation for ability, several times was about to promote him to administrator but Shu slandered him each time and it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to promote him several times; Shu blocked it each time.

sentences.zh: 大業末，乞骸骨，優詔許之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he begged to retire; a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye he retired on a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 去官之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he left office his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He left office with no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，終於家。

translations.literal: After a year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉曠，不知何許人也，性謹厚，每以誠恕應物。

translations.literal: Liu Kuang—his place of origin is unknown; by nature he was careful and generous and always responded to things with sincerity and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuang's origins are unknown; he was careful and responded with sincerity and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為平鄉令，單騎之官。

translations.literal: In the founding of Kaihuang he was Magistrate of Pingxiang, going to office alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he rode alone to office as magistrate of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 人有諍訟者，輒丁甯曉以義理，不加繩劾，各自引咎而去。

translations.literal: When people had disputes and lawsuits he would calmly explain with principle and righteousness, not adding punishment by whip; each withdrew blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: In disputes he explained principle without punishment; parties withdrew blaming themselves.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，賑施窮乏。

translations.literal: The salary he received he distributed to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his salary to the poor.

sentences.zh: 百姓感其德化，更相篤勵曰：「有君如此，何得為非？」

translations.literal: The people were moved by his transforming virtue and encouraged one another, saying: "With a lord like this, how can we do wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: People said: "With such a magistrate, how can we do wrong?"

sentences.zh: 在職七年，風教大洽。

translations.literal: Seven years in office; customs and teaching were greatly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in office; customs were greatly harmonized.

sentences.zh: 獄中無系囚，諍訟絕息，囹圄皆生草，庭可張羅。

translations.literal: In the prison there were no detained prisoners; disputes and quarrels ceased; the jails grew grass and in the courtyard one could stretch a net.
translations.idiomatic: The jail was empty; disputes ceased; grass grew in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 及去官，吏人無少長號泣，沿路將送，數百里不絕。

translations.literal: When he left office, officials and people young and old wept; along the road they escorted him for several hundred li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, people escorted him weeping for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 遷為臨潁令，清名善政為天下第一。

translations.literal: Transferred to Magistrate of Linying; pure name and good government ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Linying he ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射高熲言狀，上召之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat Gao Jiong reported his conduct; the emperor summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong reported him; the emperor summoned him.

sentences.zh: 及引見，勞之曰：「天下縣令固多矣，卿能獨異於眾，良足美也。」

translations.literal: When he was granted audience the emperor comforted him: "Magistrates in the realm are indeed many; you alone differ from the multitude—truly admirable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Magistrates are many; you alone stand apart—admirable."

sentences.zh: 顧謂侍臣曰：「若不殊獎，何以勸人？」

translations.literal: Turning to the attendant ministers he said: "If there is no special reward, how can people be encouraged?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to ministers: "Without special reward, how can we encourage others?"

sentences.zh: 於是下優詔，擢拜莒州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon a gracious edict was issued promoting him to Governor of Ju Province.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict made him governor of Ju.

sentences.zh: 王伽，河間章武人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jia was a man of Zhangwu in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia was from Zhangwu in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，為齊州參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang he was a staff officer in Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaihuang he was a Qi province staff officer.

sentences.zh: 初無足稱，後被州使送流囚李參等七十餘人詣京師。

translations.literal: At first there was nothing worth mentioning; later he was sent by the province to escort exiled prisoners Li Can and more than seventy others to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later the province sent him to escort seventy-odd exiles including Li Can to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時制，流人並枷鎖傳送。

translations.literal: The regulations at the time required exiles to be sent in cangues and chains.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required exiles to be sent in cangues and chains.

sentences.zh: 次滎陽，憫其辛苦，悉呼而謂之曰：「卿輩既犯國刑，虧損名教，身嬰縲絏，此其職也。

translations.literal: Stopping at Xingyang, he pitied their hardship, called them all and said: "You have violated the state's punishment and damaged reputation and teaching; your bodies bear fetters—this is your lot.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang he pitied them: "You broke the law and wear fetters—that is your lot.

sentences.zh: 今復重勞援卒，豈獨不愧於心哉！」

translations.literal: Now again heavily troubling the escort soldiers—is this not shameful in the heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you burden escorts again—is that not shameful?"

sentences.zh: 參等辭謝。

translations.literal: Can and the others apologized.
translations.idiomatic: They apologized.

sentences.zh: 伽曰：「汝等雖犯憲法，枷鎖亦大苦辛，吾欲與汝等脫去，行至京師總集，能不違期不？」

translations.literal: Jia said: "Though you violated the law, the cangue is also great hardship; I wish to remove them for you and walk to the capital for assembly—can you not miss the deadline?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia said: "I will remove your cangues if you reach the capital on time—can you?"

sentences.zh: 皆拜謝曰：「必不敢違。」

translations.literal: All bowed and said: "We will certainly not violate it."
translations.idiomatic: All bowed and said, "We certainly will not break faith."

sentences.zh: 伽於是悉脫枷，停援卒，與期曰：「某日當至京師。

translations.literal: Jia thereupon removed all cangues, dismissed the escort soldiers, and set a date: "On such-and-such a day we should reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He removed the cangues, dismissed escorts, and set a date, saying, "On such-and-such a day we should reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 如致前卻，吾當為汝受死。」

translations.literal: If you cause delay or retreat, I will die for you."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, I will die for you."

sentences.zh: 舍之而去。

translations.literal: He released them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He released them and left.

sentences.zh: 流人感悅，依期而至，一無離叛。

translations.literal: The exiles were moved and pleased; they arrived on schedule without a single defection.
translations.idiomatic: The exiles arrived on time without a single defection.

sentences.zh: 上聞而驚異，召見與語，稱善久之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was startled and amazed; he summoned Jia and spoke with him, praising him long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and praised him long.

sentences.zh: 於是悉召流人，並令攜負妻子俱入，賜宴於殿庭而赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the exiles and ordered them to bring wives and children into the palace; he gave a feast in the hall and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the exiles in the hall and pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「凡在有生，含靈稟性，咸知好惡，並識是非。
