translations.literal: Then he issued an edict: "All who have life, endowed with spirit and nature, all know good and evil and distinguish right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "All living beings know good and evil and right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 若臨以至誠，明加勸導，則俗必從化，人皆遷善。

translations.literal: If one faces them with utmost sincerity and clearly adds guidance and encouragement, then custom will follow transformation and all will move toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: With sincerity and guidance, custom transforms and people turn good.

sentences.zh: 往以海內亂離，德教廢絕，官人無慈愛之心，兆庶懷奸詐之意，所以獄訟不息，澆薄難理。

translations.literal: Formerly within the seas there was disorder and separation; moral teaching was cut off; officials had no hearts of kindness; the multitude harbored crafty intentions—hence lawsuits did not cease and shallowness was hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Former disorder cut off moral teaching; officials lacked kindness and lawsuits multiplied.

sentences.zh: 朕受命上天，安養萬姓，思導聖法，以德化人。

translations.literal: We received the mandate from Heaven, pacify and nurture the myriad people, think to guide the sage's law, and transform people through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We received Heaven's mandate to nurture the people and transform them through virtue.

sentences.zh: 朝夕孜孜，意本如此。

translations.literal: Morning and evening diligent—this was the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening this was our intent.

sentences.zh: 而伽深識朕意，誠心宣導。

translations.literal: Yet Jia deeply understood Our intent and sincerely proclaimed and guided.
translations.idiomatic: Jia understood this and guided sincerely.

sentences.zh: 參等感悟，自赴憲司。

translations.literal: Can and the others were moved to awareness and went themselves to the law office.
translations.idiomatic: The exiles went themselves to face the law.

sentences.zh: 明率土之人，非為難教，良是官人不加示曉，致令陷罪，無由自新。

translations.literal: Clearly the people within the four seas are not hard to teach; truly it is that officials do not show and explain, causing them to fall into guilt with no way to renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: People are not hard to teach; officials failed to guide them into guilt.

sentences.zh: 若使官盡王伽之儔，人皆李參之輩，刑措不用，其何遠哉！」

translations.literal: If officials were all like Wang Jia and people all like Li Can, punishments could be set aside unused—how far off is that!"
translations.idiomatic: If all officials were like Jia and all people like Can, punishments would fall unused!"

sentences.zh: 於是擢伽為雍令，政有能名。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia was promoted to Magistrate of Yong; his government had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was promoted to magistrate of Yong with a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 魏德深，本鉅鹿人也。

translations.literal: Wei Deshen was originally from Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Deshen was originally from Julu.

sentences.zh: 祖沖，仕周，為刑部大夫、建州刺史，因家弘農。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong served Zhou as Minister of Justice and Governor of Jian Province and settled his family in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chong served Zhou and settled the family in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 父毗，郁林令。

translations.literal: His father Pi was Magistrate of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi was magistrate of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 德深初為隋文帝挽郎，後曆馮翊郡書佐，武陽郡司戶、書佐，以能遷貴鄉長。

translations.literal: Deshen at first was a mourning officer for Emperor Wen of Sui; later he served successively as clerk of Fengyi Commandery and as household and clerk of Wuyang Commandery; for ability he was transferred to Chief of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a mourning officer, served as clerk in Fengyi and Wuyang, and became chief of Guixiang.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，不嚴而肅。

translations.literal: His government was pure and quiet; not severe yet orderly.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was quiet; not harsh yet orderly.

sentences.zh: 會興遼東之役，徵稅百端，使人往來，責成郡縣。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign arose, levies were demanded on every side; envoys came and went, holding commanderies and counties responsible.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong campaign brought levies from every side.

sentences.zh: 于時王綱弛紊，吏多贓賄，所在征斂，人不堪命。

translations.literal: At that time the royal net was slack and tangled; many officials were corrupt; wherever they were, levies and collections made life unbearable for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Law was slack; officials were corrupt; levies made life unbearable.

sentences.zh: 唯德深一縣，有無相通，不竭其力，所求皆給，而百姓不擾。

translations.literal: Only in Deshen's one county those who had and lacked communicated; they did not exhaust their strength; what was sought was all supplied yet the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Only his county shared resources, met demands, and kept the people undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊群起，武陽諸城，多被淪陷，唯貴鄉獨全。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in groups; many cities of Wuyang were overrun; only Guixiang alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits overran Wuyang cities; only Guixiang remained intact.

sentences.zh: 郡丞元寶藏受詔逐捕盜賊，每戰不利，則器械必盡，輒徵發於人，動以軍法從事，如此者數矣。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Yuan Baocang received an edict to pursue bandits; whenever battle went badly weapons were always exhausted; he then levied on the people and always applied military law—this happened several times.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Baocang lost battles and repeatedly levied the people under military law.

sentences.zh: 其鄰城營造，皆聚於査事，吏人遞相督責，晝夜喧囂，猶不能濟。

translations.literal: Neighboring cities' construction all gathered at the investigation hall; officials and people supervised one another; day and night noisy; still they could not finish.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring counties' construction crowded the hall day and night yet could not finish.

sentences.zh: 德深各問其所欲，任隨便修營，官府寂然，恆若無事。

translations.literal: Deshen asked each what they wished and let them build as convenient; the government offices were silent, always as if nothing were happening.
translations.idiomatic: Deshen let each build as they wished; his offices stayed quiet as if nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 唯約束長吏，所修不須過勝餘縣，使百姓勞苦。

translations.literal: He only restrained the chief clerks so that what they built need not exceed other counties and make the people toil.
translations.idiomatic: He restrained clerks so construction need not exceed other counties.

sentences.zh: 然在下各自竭心，常為諸縣之最。

translations.literal: Yet those below each exhausted their hearts on their own and were often foremost among the counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet subordinates strove on their own and often ranked first among counties.

sentences.zh: 尋轉館陶長，貴鄉吏人聞之，相與言及其事，皆歔欷流涕，語不成聲。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Chief of Guantao; the officials and people of Guixiang heard and together spoke of the matter, all sighing and weeping, words failing to form.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guantao, Guixiang people wept until words failed.

sentences.zh: 及將赴任，傾城送之，號泣之聲，道路不絕。

translations.literal: When he was about to take up office the whole city saw him off; sounds of wailing did not cease along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city escorted him weeping along the road.

sentences.zh: 既至館陶，闔境老幼，皆如見其父母。

translations.literal: Having reached Guantao, old and young throughout the region were as if seeing their parents.
translations.idiomatic: In Guantao old and young greeted him as parents.

sentences.zh: 有猾人員外郎趙君實，與郡丞元寶藏深相交結，前後令長，未有不受其指麾者。

translations.literal: There was a crafty man, Outer Palace Attendant Zhao Junshi, who was deeply connected with Vice Administrator Yuan Baocang; former chiefs had none who did not accept their orders.
translations.idiomatic: The crafty attendant Zhao Junshi commanded former chiefs through Baocang.

sentences.zh: 自德深至縣，君實屏處於室，未嘗輒敢出門。

translations.literal: From the time Deshen arrived at the county, Junshi hid in his room and never dared go out the door.
translations.idiomatic: After Deshen came, Junshi hid indoors and dared not go out.

sentences.zh: 逃竄之徒，歸來如市。

translations.literal: Fugitives returned like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives returned like a market.

sentences.zh: 貴鄉父老，冒涉艱險，詣闕請留德深，有詔許之。

translations.literal: The elders of Guixiang braved hardship and danger, went to the palace to request that Deshen be retained; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Guixiang elders petitioned to retain him; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 館陶父老，復詣郡相訟，以貴鄉文書為詐。

translations.literal: The elders of Guantao again went to the commandery to sue, saying the Guixiang documents were fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: Guantao elders sued, calling Guixiang's documents fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 郡不能決。

translations.literal: The commandery could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery could not decide.

sentences.zh: 會持節使者韋霽、杜整等至，兩縣詣使訟之，乃斷從貴鄉。

translations.literal: When commissioners Wei Ji and Du Zheng and others arrived, both counties went to the commissioners to litigate; they then ruled for Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners ruled for Guixiang after both counties sued.

sentences.zh: 貴鄉吏人，歌呼滿道，互相稱慶；

translations.literal: The officials and people of Guixiang sang and shouted filling the road, congratulating one another;
translations.idiomatic: Guixiang people sang and congratulated along the road;

sentences.zh: 館陶眾庶，合境悲泣，因從而居住者數百家。

translations.literal: the multitude of Guantao wept throughout the region; because of this several hundred households followed and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Guantao wept; hundreds of households followed him to dwell.

sentences.zh: 寶藏深害其能。

translations.literal: Baocang deeply resented his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Baocang deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 會越王侗徵兵于郡，寶藏遂令德深率兵千人赴東都。

translations.literal: When Prince Tong of Yue raised troops in the commandery, Baocang then ordered Deshen to lead a thousand men east to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tong raised troops, Baocang sent Deshen with a thousand men to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 俄而寶藏以武陽歸李密，德深所領皆武陽人也，以本土從賊，念其親戚，輒出都門，東向慟哭而反。

translations.literal: Soon Baocang surrendered Wuyang to Li Mi; those Deshen led were all Wuyang men; following their native place to join the bandits, thinking of their kin, they went out the capital gate, turned east, wailed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Baocang surrendered to Li Mi, Deshen's Wuyang men wept at the gate and turned back.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之曰：「李密兵馬，近在金墉，去此二十餘里，汝必欲歸，誰能相禁？

translations.literal: Someone said to them: "Li Mi's troops are near Jincheng, twenty-odd li from here; if you must return, who can forbid you? Why torment yourselves so!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "Li Mi is near—who can stop you if you return? Why torment yourselves?

sentences.zh: 何為自苦如此！」

translations.literal: Why torment yourselves so!"
translations.idiomatic: Why torment yourselves so!"

sentences.zh: 其人皆垂泣曰：「我與魏明府同來，不忍棄去，豈以道路艱難乎！」

translations.literal: Those men all wept and said: "We came with Magistrate Wei; we cannot bear to leave him—is it because the road is hard!"
translations.idiomatic: They wept: "We came with Magistrate Wei and cannot leave him—not because the road is hard!"

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: He won people's hearts to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He won hearts to this degree.

sentences.zh: 後與賊戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Later in battle with the bandits he fell in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell in battle against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 貴鄉、館陶人庶，至今懷之。

translations.literal: The people of Guixiang and Guantao to this day cherish him.
translations.idiomatic: Guixiang and Guantao people cherish him to this day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：為政之道，寬猛相濟，猶寒暑迭代，俱成歲功者也。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The way of governing balances leniency and severity, like cold and heat alternating—both complete the year's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Governance balances leniency and severity like seasons completing the year.

sentences.zh: 然存夫簡久，必藉寬平，大則致鼓腹之歡，小則有息肩之惠。

translations.literal: Yet to endure long requires leaning on leniency and peace; in great matters it brings the joy of full bellies; in small matters the grace of resting the shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Endurance requires leniency and peace; great and small both bring relief.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「雖無德與汝，式歌且舞。」

translations.literal: Hence the Odes says: "Though we have no virtue to give you, we sing and dance."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Odes: "Though we have no virtue for you, we sing and dance."

sentences.zh: 張膺等皆有寬仁之心，至誠待物，化行所屬，愛結人心，故得所去見思，所居而化。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying and the others all had hearts of generous benevolence, treating things with utmost sincerity; transformation went forth where they belonged; love bound people's hearts—hence where they left they were missed, where they dwelt they were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying and others ruled with generous sincerity; where they ruled people were transformed; where they left they were missed.

sentences.zh: 《詩》所謂「愷悌君子，人之父母」，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: What the Odes calls "the easy and pleasant gentleman, the people's father and mother"—is it mere empty talk!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' "easy and pleasant gentleman, the people's father and mother"—is no empty phrase!
